543663|2026-03.headline: Five-Star Q4 FY26: Q4 slippage fell to 0.7% from 1.9%, while FY27 AUM growth guided at ~20% and credit cost at 1.7-1.75%.
543663|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as the toughest year, with asset quality stress from MFI and unsecured overlap reaching the secured small-ticket LAP book. Q4 showed recovery: unique customer collection efficiency was 98.1%, x-bucket collections 99.3%, and slippage ratio fell to 0.7% from 1.9% in Q3. Disbursements rose 24% QoQ to INR1,213 crores and PAT was INR269 crores, down 3% QoQ on higher personnel expenses. Management guided to ~20% AUM growth in FY27 and a steady-state credit cost of 1.5-1.6% over FY28-30.

financial_highlights.change: management also cited 8.37% ROA on average AUM in the call
includes USD100mn ADB facility; USD50mn drawn

segments.name: South India (core)
segments.commentary: Around 85% or more of AUM is in the South, where over-leverage stress first appeared; management expects South to drive ~20% or more growth in FY27. Karnataka x-bucket collections were 99%.

segments.name: Non-South / new states
segments.commentary: Maharashtra operations started with branches in Nashik, Pune and Aurangabad, which lifted the Tier 1-2 share of AUM from ~1% to ~2%. Management plans to scale Maharashtra branches from ~40 to 70-80.

segments.name: Micro-LAP (INR3-5 lakh)
segments.commentary: Core product; management expects it to return to growth in a big way in FY27. Average ticket size rose from INR3.5 lakh to INR4.2 lakh YoY, and about 50%+ of AUM sits in INR3-5 lakh.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Introduced in some locations, targeting INR7-8 lakh tickets. Management says it is a secondary priority behind micro-LAP.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of around 20%, with a conservative range of 18-20%; management says close to 20% for the next two to three years.
FY27 disbursements of INR6,500-7,000 crores per the Q&A; another analyst's arithmetic used INR6,200-6,400 crores for 20% growth, which management said is achievable.
FY27 credit cost of 1.7-1.75% of average AUM; steady-state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30.
FY27 opex to average AUM of 7-7.25%, with limited scale benefit.
FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady-state ROA of 8-8.25%; spread around 13.5%.
Yield: about 30-40 bps further book-yield decline over the next 3-4 quarters; incremental lending at ~22.5%. Cost of funds: no major drop expected in FY27, with borrowing at ~8.5%.
Plan to open 60-75 branches in FY27, versus about 90-96 opened last year.
capex_capacity: Branch network: 60-75 new branches planned for FY27; 95% of branches opened last year have reached breakeven, per management.
Catchment area per branch of 25-30 km; new branches expected to break even in 9-12 months.
Business and collections teams separated and fully operational from April 1, 2026.
Write-offs for FY26 were about INR160-165 crores.
demand_pricing: April is seasonally weak; management says collections are in line with a typical April, and it expects no material deterioration.
Lead indicators are strong for disbursements; management expects Q1 FY27 disbursement growth.
Pricing was cut by 200 bps about 1.5 years ago; management sees no need to revise pricing in FY27 and expects no further cut.
Top-ups and repeat loans are 10-12% of disbursements. About 84% of Q4 collections were digital, up from 80% a year ago.
Management sees fintechs as a limited threat, given the INR4-5 lakh ticket size and roughly seven-year tenor against 6-12 months for fintech loans.
Exposure to small eateries and NRI remittance-linked borrowers is sub-1% of the portfolio, with no alarm signals so far.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost trajectory for FY27 and steady state?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guided at 1.7-1.75% (Q4 was 1.88%); steady state 1.5-1.6% for FY28-30, reflecting better buckets and a shift to slightly better-quality customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the steady-state credit cost higher than the earlier 0.8-1% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Earlier guidance was on total assets (0.8-1%), roughly 1.3-1.35% on AUM. Management says it now expects to run at higher credit costs to avoid pressure on the field force while maintaining growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ROA outlook depend on margin given the steady-state credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 ROA of 8.25-8.5% and steady state of 8-8.25%. Leverage is currently low and will weigh on ROA but support ROE; spread is around 13.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 personal expense a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a combination of collections-vertical build-out and seasonal Q4 incentives. It said this is business as usual, not a one-off, and added that the April increment will also add cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can AUM growth stay at ~20% beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims for close to 20% for the next two to three years, with an 18-20% range. Growth is to be supported by pent-up demand and a low base; FY27 AUM is expected to reach about INR16,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How much yield is left to reprice on the book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 30-40 bps more book-yield decline over 3-4 quarters. Incremental lending is at ~22.5%, book yield ~22-22.25%, and Q4 yield ~22.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost of funds and rating-upgrade expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Excluding ADB, Q4 cost of funds was ~8.25-8.3%. Management expects FY27 borrowing at ~8.5% and no rating upgrade until the second half of the year, with about 30-40 bps more book-yield benefit over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Stage-2 provision coverage below the RBI 5% norm a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ECL framework for banks starts April 2027 and does not expect the 5% Stage-2 norm for NBFCs soon. It is being conservative on credit cost and may see benefit if DPDs improve.

risks_watch: Stage-2 coverage fell as the 61-90 DPD bucket dropped from 5.1% to 4.8%; management tracks overall coverage instead.
Geopolitical stress (West Asia conflict) and liquidity in the borrowing market; management expects no major cost-of-funds benefit in FY27.
Disbursement ramp needs to rise from INR1,213 crores in Q4 to INR1,400-1,500 crores per quarter; April borrowing was zero given strong liquidity.
Senior management exit during FY26; management says there is no impact on performance.
Opex to AUM is guided at 7-7.25%, above historical levels, with competition for talent.
Rating upgrade is not expected until the second half of FY27 at the earliest.

It was more cautious on cost of funds, liquidity and geopolitics, and evasive on the reason for a lower long-term growth rate versus the earlier ~25% framing.

rows.why: Book yield is ~22-22.25% against Q4 yield of ~22.6%, and incremental lending is at ~22.5%, so yield keeps compressing even though no further pricing cut is planned.

rows.why: Management said leverage is currently low and will weigh on ROA while supporting ROE; FY27 ROA is guided to 8.25-8.5%.

543663|2026-06.headline: Five-Star Q1 FY27 disbursements hit a record INR 1,496 crore (+23% QoQ, +16% YoY) while AUM grew 4% QoQ to INR 13,722 crore.
543663|2026-06.overview: Management reported a record quarterly disbursement of INR 1,496 crore and AUM of INR 13,722 crore, up 4% QoQ. Asset quality metrics improved modestly: 1+ current book rose to 83.30%, 30+ fell to 12.38%, and the 1.85% credit cost was slightly lower QoQ, while slippages were flat at 0.70%. Management guided to lower credit costs and NPLs in coming quarters, with opex staying flat in FY27 on an employee-cost reset. Q&A focused on yield compression, cost of borrowing, write-off run-rate, opex, and the timeline to higher leverage.

financial_highlights.change: Average cost of funds down ~15 bps, spread up 3 bps
Recoveries ~INR 35 crore incl. write-off and NPA settlements (vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4)

segments.name: Micro LAP (core product)
segments.commentary: Onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); management sees yield settling near 22.25% after 10-15 bps further compression over next couple of quarters. Average ticket size ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, targeting 25/50/25 mix across ~INR 3 lakh, ~INR 5 lakh and ~INR 10 lakh tickets.

segments.name: Housing loans
segments.commentary: Launched about two quarters ago; management said focus has been on restoring micro LAP before pushing housing.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of ~20% reiterated; management expects FY27 disbursements of INR 6,500-6,800 crore (Q1 run-rate plus ~10%).
FY27 credit cost guided at 1.7%-1.9%; management said the trend is more likely toward 1.7%. Overall ECL coverage to be maintained at ~1.75%-1.8%.
Gross NPA to fall to sub-3% and a steady-state NPA of ~2.5%; steady-state Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%.
Write-offs for FY27 guided at INR 225-250 crore (~INR 55-60 crore per quarter).
Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% in FY27, moving to 5.25%-5.5% from FY28. Branch additions run-rate ~50-60 per year.
Incremental cost of borrowing guided at ~8.5%; spreads expected flat for next few quarters absent policy action. Repo rate increases are a downside risk.
FY28 credit cost expected at ~1.6%-1.7%. Debt-to-equity of 2x expected in 6-8 quarters; ROA steady state 6%-6.5% and ROE 18%-20% at ~3x leverage.
Management plans to launch one more product (beyond micro LAP and housing) within ~3-6 months, with details to be shared later.
capex_capacity: Branch network at ~856 after adding ~12 in Q1, mainly in Maharashtra and newer states; FY27 additions expected at ~50-60 branches.
Collections and business functions separated into different verticals; management says this lifted productivity without any change in credit filters.
Liquidity: ~INR 1,850 crore held on balance sheet at quarter end; ~INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and ~INR 450 crore raised in Q1.
Pending ADB tranche (ECB) to be raised, with hedging cost impact; timing to be managed.
demand_pricing: Management says demand was never the constraint; the slowdown over the past 3-4 quarters came from tighter approvals and deliberate disbursement pacing.
June disbursements were ~INR 670 crore; management expects a new normal of ~INR 600-650 crore per month on average, with intra-quarter seasonality being reduced.
Repeat-customer policy relaxed: top-up offered to best customers instead of requiring full prepayment, which management expects to reduce the repayment rate from ~30% toward 27-28%.
Microfinance overlap with Five-Star customers fell from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (per management, not measured for Q1).
Competition: management cited new competitors entering, requiring more competitive employee compensation.

qa_highlights.question: Renish (ICICI): Where will cost-to-assets settle and when does operating leverage kick in?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex to stay largely flat in FY27 with 20-21% YoY growth due to competitive employee pay; cost-to-assets ~5.75%-6% this year, moving to 5.25%-5.5% in steady state from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: Has yield repricing largely finished, and what is the current lending rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Large part of contraction done; onboarding yields average ~22.5% (range 21.5%-23%); a further 10-15 bps compression expected over next couple of quarters, settling near 22.25% after NPA interest reversals.

qa_highlights.question: Viral Shah (IIFL): Further Stage 3 flow-through expected, any ARC sales, and rollback rates in early buckets?
qa_highlights.answer: No ARC sales. Slippages expected to trend down; recoveries ~INR 35 crore vs INR 26-27 crore in Q4. Rollbacks ~4-5% in 1-60 DPD buckets and ~2-3% in 61-90 DPD; management frames it as stabilisation, with unique customer collection efficiency key.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit Tibrewal (Motilal Oswal): How many more quarters until slippages decline and what is a normalised slippage rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects slippages, credit cost and NPLs to trend down in September, December and March quarters; credit cost trending toward 1.7%. Will wait 1-2 quarters of slippage trend before giving a steady-state slippage number.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What drives the disbursement acceleration (demand, approvals, productivity, geography)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand was never the constraint; earlier slowdown reflected tighter approvals and deliberate pacing. Vertical split of business and collections lifted productivity with no change in credit filters; login and sanction traction strong.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijit: What is the outlook for cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing ~8.5%, leaving room for 20-30 bps further compression on the book; pending ADB ECB tranche carries hedging cost; assumes no repo hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Chandrasekhar Sridhar (Fidelity): Is gold loan growth masking underlying stress via repayments by overlapping customers? Also ticket size and diversification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says gold loans are fully secured and repayments via gold loans are seasonal; microfinance overlap down from ~20-21% to ~16-17% (not measured for Q1). Ticket size mix target 25/50/25 across ~INR 3 lakh, 5 lakh, 10 lakh; one more product within 3-6 months. Spreads to stay flat for next few quarters absent policy action.

qa_highlights.question: Raghav Garg (Ambit): Why have repayment rates risen, and how does that reconcile with a rising 3-5 year duration share?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose on stronger collections and a policy change: top-up offered to best customers instead of full prepayment. Repayment rate currently ~30%, expected to trend to 27-28%; behavioural tenor ~4-4.5 years. Management said 85-90% of loans are disbursed on 7-year tenure; the vintage shift reflects seasoning and higher disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: Rajiv Mehta (Yes Securities): Trajectory of write-offs, coverage build-back, and FY28 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 write-offs guided INR 225-250 crore, roughly flat at ~INR 55-60 crore per quarter; steady-state write-off view in 2-3 quarters. Overall ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%, whichever mix of Stage 1/2/3. FY28 credit cost ~1.6-1.7%. Growth achieved with no change in credit filters.

qa_highlights.question: Kunal Shah (Citi): Steady-state bucket mix and employee cost drivers, attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state: Stage 1 ~91-92%, Stage 2 ~6-7%, Stage 3 ~2.5%; current book to reach ~85% by end FY27 from 83.3%; 30+ below 12%. Employee cost rise is salary realignment and incentives for branch staff, not ESOPs. Attrition flat so far; trends in 2-3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Nischint (Kotak): Expense growth this year and whether 20% loan growth guidance stands?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth ~20-21% YoY, similar to Q1; increments and appraisals already in Q1 base. ECL coverage ~1.75-1.8%; write-offs INR 55-60 crore per quarter; 20% AUM growth guidance reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Divyansh Gupta (Latent PMS): Why did debt decline from March, cost of funds for levering up, and timing of D/E of 2x?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 borrowing was muted as banks awaited results; INR 1,000 crore raised in Q4 and INR 450 crore in Q1; INR 1,850 crore liquidity held. Guide 8.5% incremental cost. D/E of 2x in 6-8 quarters, as net worth adds ~INR 1,100-1,200 crore PAT annually.

qa_highlights.question: Chirag Fialoke (MS Capital): Are incremental disbursements averaging INR 5-7 lakh, and what is the 60-90 DPD bucket?
qa_highlights.answer: Average ticket ~INR 4.5-5 lakh, expected to hold around INR 5 lakh; mix guidance unchanged. Management deferred the 60-90 DPD figure to the IR team.

qa_highlights.question: Darshan Deora (Indvest): Steady-state ROE target, and will yields be raised back given higher collection costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Current ROA ~8-8.5% on AUM (7-7.25% on total assets); steady-state ROA 6-6.5% and ROE 18-20% at ~3x leverage. Management says the cost increase will be recovered through lower credit cost, not higher lending rates; the 200 bps cut in Oct 2024 tracked borrowing costs falling from 11%+.

qa_highlights.question: Renish: What was June disbursement and is INR 600-650 crore a monthly run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: June disbursements ~INR 670 crore; management is working to reduce intra-quarter seasonality and agreed an average of ~INR 600-650 crore per month is a fair assumption for the rest of the year.

risks_watch: Yield compression: onboarding yields ~22.5% with a further 10-15 bps decline expected over the next couple of quarters, and NPA interest reversals weigh on yields.

Cost of borrowing: guidance of ~8.5% incremental assumes no repo hikes; a rate increase or ADB ECB hedging costs would hit spreads. Management flagged energy costs and possible regulatory liquidity moves.

Asset quality: slippages flat QoQ at 0.70%; credit cost guidance 1.7-1.9% and gross NPA sub-3% depend on slippages turning down in September, December and March quarters. Write-off run-rate ~INR 60 crore per quarter gives little relief in FY27.
Opex and employee cost: opex growth 20-21% YoY and cost-to-assets ~5.75-6% in FY27; attrition is flat and too early to call, with more competitors entering.
Disbursement sustainability: H1 run-rate of ~INR 600-650 crore per month and reliance on a new product within 3-6 months; leverage target of 2x D/E is 6-8 quarters away.
key_quotes: We clocked our historical best in disbursement with quarterly disbursements coming in at INR 1,496 crores, a growth of 23% over the previous quarter and 16% over the previous year.
So our request is, can you please keep yourself mute so that the background noise is too much.
So it's not like we are completely removing the DNA of collections from the business people.
Srikanth Gopalakrishnan: Interest reversals on NPAs, Renish.

543663|2026-09.headline: Five-Star Q2 FY27: record disbursements of Rs 2,078 crore (+74% YoY) and PAT of Rs 299 crore, but management flags spread compression ahead.
543663|2026-09.overview: Disbursements hit a historical high of Rs 2,078 crore, up 39% QoQ and 74% YoY, while AUM reached Rs 14,640 crore (+14% YoY). Collection efficiency improved to 98.2% and 30+ DPD fell to 11.5% from 12.38%, though GNPA was sticky at 3.48%. PAT was Rs 299 crore, including a Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit (about Rs 281 crore underlying). Management guided to tighter spreads as cost of funds rises, partly offset by a roughly 1% yield hike on incremental loans effective October 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 299 crore (Rs 281 crore excluding Rs 19 crore one-time tax benefit)
about 7.5% in Q2; about 7.35-7.40% for the year

segments.name: Core geographies (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana)
segments.commentary: Together more than 80% of AUM; management reports no drought-like stress and collections holding up. Tamil Nadu collects best, followed by Andhra and Telangana.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Management says collections are improving month-on-month after the state ordinance impact, and disbursements are being pushed more firmly there.

segments.name: Ticket-size mix (disbursements)
segments.commentary: Sub Rs 3 lakh about 26-27%, Rs 3-5 lakh about 51-52%, above Rs 5 lakh the balance. Target steady state is about 25/50/25.

guidance_outlook: Expect flattish credit slippages and credit cost for the rest of FY27; slippage around 70 bps for the next couple of quarters.
Incremental yields up about 1% from October 2026, but absorbing it across the book will take roughly 24-36 months (about 8 quarters per management on one question).
Incremental cost of borrowings expected 8.70-8.75% in H2 FY27; book cost of funds to exit FY27 about 12-15 bps higher, near 8.90%.
Spread compression expected: about 10-12 bps for H1 and about 10-15 bps by FY27 exit; margin expansion ruled out.
Growth guidance to be comfortably exceeded; any revised guidance likely after Q3. Opex to AUM to fall 50-75 bps over the next couple of years, to 6.75-7%.
October disbursements about Rs 550 crore (muted), with November and December expected to pick up.
capex_capacity: Added 19 branches in Q2 and 75 over the last year, focused on deepening presence in core geographies.
Active loans about 5.1 lakh, up 5% YoY.
Liquidity about Rs 1,300 crore at September 30; unavailed sanctions about Rs 1,100 crore.
Raised incremental debt of Rs 825 crore at an all-in cost of 8.43%; bank borrowings about 69% of total (67% in Q1).
Second tranche of ADB facility still pending, with hedging cost on the higher side.
demand_pricing: Customer rates raised about 1% on incremental disbursements across risk categories, from about 21-23% to about 22.5-23.9%, effective October 2026.
Top-up loans are about 10-15% of disbursements (Rs 200-300 crore per quarter); incremental top-up disbursal about 50% of the outstanding.
Management says yield hikes will not raise defaults, citing that loans above Rs 5 lakh earlier carried the same yield as sub-Rs 3 lakh loans.
Insurance commission impact from the IRDAI circular is nil, as Five-Star passes insurance premiums through without earning commission.
Gold loan overlap: 40-50% of customers have some gold loan; meaningful overlap about 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: How will asset quality move given the rainfall deficit, and any stress signs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no drought stress in core states; collections in October are in line with July and September, with October D1C1 expected near 98%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the behavioural tenure?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayment rises due to adjusting outstanding on internal top-ups (about 1-2% extra repayments); behavioural tenure to move closer to 4 years, from the 36-37% repayment rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much have customer rates been raised, and when does yield bottom?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1% on incremental disbursements; management agreed that yields have bottomed this quarter, but margin expansion is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the write-off recovery trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Recoveries take about 18-24 months given no SARFAESI access on loans below Rs 20 lakh; H1 recoveries were about Rs 20 crore and NPA resolutions Rs 35 crore in Q2 (Rs 25 crore in Q1).

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds and spread move?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost of borrowing to rise 20-25 bps vs Q2, with book cost up 12-15 bps by FY27 exit; H1 spread hit about 10-12 bps, roughly 8 bps post-tax.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Legal expenses from the scaled-up legal recovery vertical and CSR spend based on the 3-year average profit.

risks_watch: Rate cycle: a further 25-50 bp repo hike would add to cost of funds beyond the 10-15 bps built in; December policy is a key watch point.

543687|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 20% to Rs 1,138 crore and EBITDA 34% to Rs 101 crore, while branded formulation grew only 3%.

Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 234 crore (+11% YoY) against a stronger base. Growth was driven by domestic institutional formulation (+15%), exports recovery and a 37% rise in domestic active ingredient sales, while branded formulation was muted at 3% due to uneven monsoon and channel destocking. qa_highlights.question: Impact of El Nino and monsoon on H1 FY27 demand?

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers and margins?

543687|2026-09.headline: Dharmaj Crop Guard cut FY27 growth guidance to single-digit from 18-20%, as Q2 revenue fell 4% to Rs 332.6 crore on a weak monsoon and technical slump.
543687|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue held flat at Rs 716.7 crore and PAT rose 3% to Rs 51.3 crore, but Q2 revenue fell 4% YoY and EBITDA margin compressed to 7.3% from 9.2%. Management attributed the weakness to an 87% of LPA monsoon, a technical business down 27% in Q2 on West Asia-linked input cost and demand disruption, and higher raw material costs flowing through COGS. FY27 revenue guidance was reduced to single-digit growth from the earlier 18-20%. Management reiterated the Rs 2,000 crore revenue target for 2030 and said the herbicide facility remains on track.

segments.commentary: Grew 2% YoY in Q2 and 3% in H1; contributed 55% of H1 FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Branded (blended) formulation
segments.commentary: Grew 5% YoY in Q2 and 2% in H1 as weak Kharif farmer consumption held back growth; contributed 19% of H1 revenue.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Flat YoY in Q2; H1 export grew 50% YoY to Rs 60 crore, now 8% of revenue vs 6% last year.

segments.name: Technical
segments.commentary: Revenue down 27% YoY in Q2 and 20% in H1 on West Asia-linked input pricing and demand disruption; 18% of H1 revenue vs 22% a year earlier. Production aligned to captive formulation needs.

Management expects to restore technical margins through cost pass-through to customers over Q3 FY27.
H2 focus: push higher exports, sustain domestic formulation, and restore technical margins.
Dharmaj 2030 target of Rs 2,000 crore revenue reconfirmed; management says it is on track, with about three years left.
Herbicide facility near Ahmedabad (Kerala GIDC) remains on track for commissioning, with production cycle ahead of next Kharif season.
capex_capacity: Capital work-in-progress Rs 11.7 crore at 30 Sep 2026 vs Rs 6.2 crore at March 2026, reflecting spend on the herbicide facility.
New herbicide facility to release capacity at the existing site; herbicide production cycle begins ahead of next Kharif.
Technical capacity aligned to captive formulation requirement to keep plant utilised; three new technical products added, with 2-3 products now backward-integrated.

Technical market hit by West Asia crisis affecting input prices and demand; merchant market realisation described as steady.

Operating expenses down 14% YoY to Rs 37.6 crore in Q2, partly offsetting gross margin compression.
Management says there is no sales return policy and no significant channel inventory issue.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned for FY28 and how will formulation growth return?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Agarwal said the weak season is rainfall-driven and the company remains on track for Rs 2,000 crore by 2030. Ramesh Talavia said the rainfall shortfall was mainly in Western India, with East and North not affected, and that the company will focus on recovering there.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be channel returns or inventory pressure given the sector downturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Talavia said company policy is no sales returns and it controls this by working to need-based orders. He said there is no major inventory issue and that the company expects single-digit growth by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What technical molecules and geographies are targeted to support the Rs 2,000 crore vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Talavia said R&D and pilot work has added three new technical products, with 2-3 already backward-integrated. Priority is captive consumption for B2C and B2B formulations, with small technical sales. Export registrations have started coming in.

Herbicide facility commissioning timeline and its ramp-up before next Kharif.
Working capital: inventory fell to Rs 174 crore and receivables to Rs 409.9 crore; monitor for collection stress in a weak season.
Export momentum must be sustained to offset weak technical and branded volumes.

543689|2026-03.headline: Uniparts Q4 FY26 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR339 crores with EBITDA margin of 24%; management guides FY27 growth in line with FY26's 21%.

FY26 revenue grew 21%, above the mid-teens guidance given earlier. Management said the agriculture and construction cycle is turning, with new business wins of over INR225 crores annualised in the trailing 12 months. A fire at the Ludhiana finishing shop in Q3 was handled via interim arrangements and is covered by insurance, with normal operations expected by year-end. Management said the company remains net debt free with INR160 crores net cash.

543714|2026-06.headline: Landmark Cars Q1 FY27 pro forma revenue grew over 22% YoY to a record Q1, with PAT nearly doubling; EBITDA margin about 5.8%.
543714|2026-06.overview: Management reported its best-ever Q1 on pro forma revenue from operations, up over 22% YoY in a seasonally soft quarter, with PAT nearly doubling. Management attributed roughly 19 percentage points of growth to volume and about 3 points to OEM price hikes. Management said it will judge the business on EBITDA, PAT and cash profit rather than gross profit, given the mix shift toward newer brands with different margin structures. Q&A covered EV aftersales economics, the ChargeZone charging partnership, workshop capacity (expressed in bays rather than outlet count), rental costs and cost efficiency. Management gave no numeric quantification for the ChargeZone revenue share or for FY28 profit targets.

Management expects a normalised ~1.5% EBITDA margin on pro forma new car sales in Q2-Q4 FY27 when asked.

segments.commentary: Management said aftersales is growing at about 14-15% historically; EV aftersales revenue per vehicle is higher, with EV margins (ex-warranty) similar to the ~15% currently cited, and not expected to be lower. Share of aftersales from high-growth brands is 19% vs 38% of new car sales from those brands, per analyst.

Borrowing costs described as stable; surplus cash to be used to repay working capital loans.

Management argued that competition such as Audi's share push expands the luxury market (about 50,000 units) rather than cannibalises it.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said new entrants expand the luxury market; the segment has hovered near 50,000 units and luxury penetration fell last year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ChargeZone partnership add revenue, and at what economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ChargeZone runs about 16,000 charging points; Landmark onboards EV customers and earns a recurring revenue share with wallet credits for customers. Commercials were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2-Q4 to be normalised, with an EBITDA margin around 1.5% on pro forma new car sales; Q1 is seasonally the weakest quarter and Mercedes grew strongly YoY.

543720|2026-03.headline: KFin Q4 FY26 revenue rose 23% YoY (4.6% ex-Ascent) as mark-to-market hits and weak Issuer Solutions held EBITDA margin to 37%; FY27 guide 23-24% revenue growth.
543720|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew about 23% YoY but fell 6.3% QoQ, and ex-Ascent growth was only 4.6% YoY. Mark-to-market losses on equity and metal-ETF-driven asset mix shifts, plus weaker Issuer Solutions retail folios and corporate actions, weighed on the quarter. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 37% in Q4 (ex-Ascent about 42%), and core PAT rose 3.8% YoY in the quarter and 6.2% for FY26 to INR353 crore. Management guided to conservative FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 23-24%, EBITDA growth of 16-17% (margin near 39-40%) and PAT growth of about 10%, and said it will recalibrate monthly.

segments.name: Domestic mutual fund

AUM grew in line with industry at about 21%, but revenue grew about 11% due to April 2025 pricing discounts, MTM erosion and ETF mix shift.

segments.name: Issuer Solutions
segments.commentary: Contributes 10% of Q4 revenue; both revenue and segment profit fell YoY. Management cited retail folio exodus (existing clients lost about 1.7 million folios vs 2.5-3 million added through new wins), tepid corporate actions and a base effect from a large Q4 FY25 demerger.

segments.name: AIF, private wealth and PMS
segments.commentary: Contributes 4.5% of Q4 revenue. AIF AUM grew about 19-24% and AIF fund count rose from 593 to 741, with margins above 37%; private wealth/PMS revenue fell on MTM, though 6 wealth platform wins were signed early in the year.

segments.commentary: Contributes 4.5% of Q4 revenue; management guides about 60%+ GFS growth next year, citing large RTA and fund accounting deal wins in the last three quarters, including the Philippines largest bank fund accounting contract.

segments.name: Ascent Fund Solutions (acquired October)
segments.commentary: Contributes about 15% of Q4 revenue at 8% EBITDA margin; about 499 new fund-manager clients added (about 900-950 funds). Management expects Ascent revenue growth of 25-30% and margin to move to the early teens over time.

segments.name: NPS, Reval, Hexagram
segments.commentary: Each about 1.5% of Q4 revenue. NPS AUM-linked pricing moved from per-subscriber to basis points, and pension subscribers grew about 34% vs industry 11%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 23-24% (CFO also cited 24-25% in Q&A); management stressed this is not formal guidance.

International organic revenue expected to grow over 60% and total international revenue over 70% including Ascent this year.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic MF yield decline of about 4-5% YoY in FY27 still hold if metal mix stabilises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance assumes the same asset mix as end-FY26 with ETFs around 23%; it expects more active funds this year, and the 4-5% yield view was not directly reconfirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is steady-state Issuer Solutions revenue growth after one-offs, given realisations hit harder than folios?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to net folio loss (about 1.7 million existing folios lost), weak corporate actions in Q4, and a demerger base effect; it expects these to normalise from Q1 FY27 with demergers pushed from March into May.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Ascent's EBITDA-to-PAT gap widen, and is the company paying tax despite losses at Ascent?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the gap is amortisation of acquired client contracts and brand (about INR6 crore a quarter, 10-year life); operating leverage should offset it over 2-3 years. Ascent's top-line growth is 5% in USD, about 8% in INR QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why does FY27 EBITDA guidance imply margin below 40% after Ascent consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the implied margin is about 39%, but it still aims for above 40% through cost productivity, with new-business drag and BD spend included; it expects the range to be 40-45% over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did alternatives, private wealth and PMS revenue fall QoQ, and why is Ascent yield below its earlier 8-9 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Private wealth/PMS fell on MTM markdowns and deferred Q3/Q4 deals; AIF AUM grew 24-25%. Ascent yield was always about 7 bps per management, moving with asset mix such as crypto funds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for KRA revenue and Aladdin integration?
qa_highlights.answer: KRA went live late Q3/early Q4 FY26 with over 25 AMCs and brokers signed; a proposed single POS KYC ID could reduce fetch-cost revenue industry-wide. Aladdin integration is slower, with direct integration and BD expected in a couple of quarters.

543720|2026-06.headline: KFin Q1 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY to consolidate Ascent (ex-Ascent ~10%), while PAT was flat-to-down and EBITDA margin fell to 34.2% with Ascent.
543720|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 30% YoY, with about 9.6% growth excluding Ascent, and 2.7% QoQ including Ascent (1.6% excluding). EBITDA grew about 7.1% YoY, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 34.2% with Ascent versus 39.4% without it. PAT margin was 21% including Ascent and 26.6% excluding it, and PAT was broadly flat to marginally down YoY. Management raised its FY27 growth outlook to EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, while a yield decline of about 2% QoQ in mutual funds was attributed to debt-to-liquid mix shift and provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

financial_highlights.change: About INR 200 crore to go to dividend already declared

financial_highlights.value: About 51% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow

financial_highlights.change: from US$5.7 million in Q4; US$4.4 million in Q1 FY26 (pre-consolidation), +32% YoY

segments.name: Domestic mutual fund (RTA/fund admin)
segments.commentary: Industry AUM grew about 15% YoY versus KFin about 16%; KFin's equity AUM market share rose about 80 bps QoQ. Yield fell about 2% QoQ, of which about 30% was debt-to-liquid mix and the rest mainly provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

segments.name: Issuer solutions
segments.commentary: Managed about 80% of main-board IPO issue size in Q1 and holds about 50% of NSE 500 market share (versus ~52% earlier). Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue; the company guided to tepid corporate actions in Q2 due to IT services dividend deferrals.

segments.commentary: Revenue up about 200% YoY with Ascent and about 32% organically. Ascent EBITDA margin was about 8%; management targets double-digit margin within 12 months. Sequential decline ex-Ascent was attributed to pipeline timing, with growth expected above 25%.

segments.commentary: About 731 funds with about 37.3% market share, targeting close to 40% with pending launches. 15 new AIF wins in Q1; the AIF business has compounded above 60% over four years and management expects at least 40% growth going forward.

segments.name: Pensions (NPS)
segments.commentary: Reached break-even last quarter and now contributes about 15%+ EBITDA margin. Manages about 2.5 million pensioners and is the second-largest CRA in India.

segments.name: Wealth management (mPower Wealth) and technology
segments.commentary: Three wealth platform mandates won. An INR 25 crore+ big-data mandate runs over about 18 months, with INR 40 crore of signed bolt-on deals across 3-15 month durations.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR guided at 18-20%, unchanged from prior guidance.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 40-45%; management aims to hold 40% threshold including Ascent by end of FY27.
FY27 visibility of EBITDA growth of about 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, ahead of the earlier high-single to low-double-digit indication.
Ascent to become EBITDA accretive by end-FY27 or early FY28; double-digit margin targeted within the next 12 months; KFin-level EBITDA margin expansion to take three to five years.

Cayman Islands facility being set up to meet regulatory substance requirements, a near-term cost already in the plan.

Ascent revenue hit by digital-asset fund markdowns, offset by six new fund managers with over US$100 million each (transitions taking 3-5 months) and fund launches.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik (Indus Capital): What cost takeouts drove better domestic MF segment margins despite single-digit revenue growth and yield compression, and can segment margins bottom out if yields stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited technology-led cost optimisation across payroll, non-payroll and licensing, not ad-hoc cuts; full increments were given this year. It said yield is driven by pricing/discounts, asset mix and AMC growth, and that pricing-driven stability is expected from here, with the SIP automation and next FinEx launch (by end calendar 2026) as controllable margin levers.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik: how much of the PAT gap (about INR 47 million between INR 799 million and INR 752 million) narrows via cost takeouts versus revenue growth, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is both, weighted more to top-line growth at Ascent (EBITDA about 7-8%), while KFin-level cost optimisation will do the heavy lifting. PAT pressure is largely non-cash amortisation of goodwill/contract payments and capitalised One Constellation platform costs.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab Mukherjee (360 ONE): Is the yield drop only debt-to-liquid mix, how should yield be modelled over the remaining three quarters given ~2% QoQ fall, and how will bolt-on wins add revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity mix was stable and the shift was debt to liquid (debt yields 2-2.5x liquid), plus provisioning for a large renewal this year. It declined to guide a yield number, saying conservatism means sticking to about 3% annual decline, though a reversal could give an upside surprise. Bolt-on deals of about INR 40 crore signed in Q1 run for 3, 6 and 15 months and are episodic, not annuity.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab: why did international ex-Ascent revenue fall QoQ, and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Mathur said the decline reflects contracts in the pipeline that will materialise in coming quarters, not a fundamental change. He expects growth above 25% and called it a one-quarter phenomenon.

qa_highlights.question: Arjun Bagga (DSP MF): what is the split of the yield decline between debt-to-liquid mix and renegotiation provisions, and will Ascent margins reach double digits next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of the 2% yield decline came from debt-to-liquid; the remaining ~1.7% was net of asset-class moves, mainly provisioning for pending renegotiation, partly offset by ETF-to-equity movement. Double-digit Ascent margin is targeted within the next 12 months, not next quarter; the QoQ fall reflected crypto fund markdowns offset by new wins and fund launches. On discounts, management said it will be harder on client discount negotiations given infrastructure cost pressure.

qa_highlights.answer: Six new fund managers with over $100 million each were won; these are transitions from incumbents, taking 3-5 months. The INR 25 crore data mandate is a single client with two contracts over about 18 months, milestone-based. 543896|2026-09.headline: Avalon Technologies Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37.4% YoY to Rs 525 crore, PAT up 59.5% to Rs 40 crore, and FY27 growth guidance raised to around 30%.

Management announced a 25-acre Orgadam (SIPCOT, Tamil Nadu) campus MoU and a 51:49 JV with Zolner Electronic AG, backed by a proposed warrant issue of up to Rs 425 crore to Zolner. Working capital days improved to 120 and ROCE rose to 24.2%, while H1 capex of Rs 90 crore included about Rs 35 crore of land.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Zolner JV's option structure?

543904|2026-03.headline: Mankind Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to INR3,443 crores with adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.1%; FY27 guided to double-digit growth.
543904|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 11.8% YoY to INR3,443 crores, led by 13.4% domestic growth, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 400 bps to 27.1% on better gross margin, operating leverage and a lower Q4 base. Full-year FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR14,278 crores, but PAT fell 3.4% to INR1,938 crores as finance cost, depreciation and lower other income weighed. Management said acute therapies were muted during FY26 but recovered sequentially from Q2, and chronic share rose to about 39-40%. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of at least double digits and adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.5-26.5%, with an effective tax rate stepping up to 25-26%.

segments.name: Domestic formulations (ex-Consumer Healthcare)

segments.name: Acute therapies
segments.commentary: Gastro outperformed IPM at 1.1x (Pantakind 1.4x); gynaecology +10.8% with Dydrogesterone +20%; vitamins and minerals +12.5%. Management expects acute to grow in line with IPM in FY27.

segments.name: BSV specialty (domestic)

segments.commentary: Q4 OTC revenue INR213 crores (+20%), with modern trade and e-commerce +57%. Share of e-commerce and modern trade rose from about 9% in FY25 to 13% in FY26. FY26 OTC INR879 crores (+9%).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Q4 exports INR557 crores (+4%), hit by geopolitical headwinds and BSV exposure in LATAM, RCIS and the Philippines. FY26 international INR2,061 crores (+35%). Management expects high double-digit growth in FY27 for both international business units.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at double digits or better, with aspiration to outperform IPM (IQVIA).
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided at 25.5% to 26.5%, better than FY26's 25.4%, with caveats on geopolitics and market conditions.
FY27 effective tax rate expected at 25% to 26%, up from 15-16% in FY26, as the Sikkim tax exemption ends.
Capex guidance of 6% to 7% of FY27 revenue, driven by the new Vadodara biotech facility; board approved up to INR500 crores investment in Mankind Medicare for this.

demand_pricing: Price increase for FY26 was 4.2% per IQVIA versus about 4.4% for the industry.

GLP-1: pen launched about one month before the call, targeting endocrinologists first; management said it is not launching vials or cutting prices.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Top-line growth guided to double digits, with aspiration to outperform IQVIA; EBITDA margin guided at 25.5-26.5%.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 spreads and EBITDA margin expected between Q1 and Q2 levels (Q3 closer to Q1; Q4 closer to Q2), with Q4 supported by seasonal demand and 11 MW solar and knitting benefits.
FY28 revenue of about INR1,800 crores considered very likely by management, after an analyst extrapolated H1 run-rate; management said this was not formal guidance.
Long-term goal of INR2,500 crores revenue at 15–18% EBITDA margin by FY30 reiterated.
Management said Q1 and Q2 margins are largely sustainable given vertical integration, green power, product mix and FTA tailwinds, though higher raw material prices will take time to absorb.
Management does not currently plan a share buyback; capital will go into growth.
capex_capacity: Of INR1,035 crores committed under the Tamil Nadu MoU, INR675 crores has been invested; the balance (about INR360–400 crores) is under discussion with the state government for incentive eligibility, with a capital subsidy of about INR145 crores mentioned by an analyst.

New INR410 crore board-approved project (includes working capital margin money) for 58,368 spindles and 5 MW rooftop solar; expected revenue INR400–420 crores at 14–15% EBITDA margin. Completion by end FY28, full benefit in FY29.
Knitting expansion: all 40 machines to be in place by Q3 FY27, with benefits from Q4 FY27. Incremental knitting capex about INR7–8 crores.
11 MW ground solar expected to be commissioned by end Q3 (December 2026), taking total green energy to 76 MW; capex about INR32 crores.

PM MITRA Park: 56 acres allotted; processing unit capex of INR275–300 crores, expected commissioning around FY30 due to SIPCOT common infrastructure delays. Total land bank about 250 acres; surplus land book value about INR100 crores.
demand_pricing: Domestic cotton rose from about INR64,000/candy to INR69,000/candy during the quarter and has been around INR67,000 since, now at parity with global cotton.
Buyers limited purchases to immediate needs when cotton and yarn prices spiked late in Q2; management said domestic demand remains steady with strong order flow.
Government removed import duty on cotton, extended to December 2026; management says imported inventory build in the next three months will be limited.
UK and New Zealand FTAs are in force (benefits expected in about a year); India-EU agreement expected to be operational in early 2027; Oman FTA also mentioned.
Lower cotton inventory provided a gain that management described as not sizable. Working capital rise was mainly cotton advances, per CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further expansions beyond 58,000 spindles, and when will projects come on stream?

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for spreads and demand?

qa_highlights.question: What were the drivers of margin expansion and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers cited: higher fabric share, lower power costs from green energy, product optimisation with strategic customers, market tailwinds and some benefit from lower cotton inventory. Management believes Q1–Q2 margins are largely sustainable.

qa_highlights.question: How much was spent on the fire and is it insured?

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,850 crore FY28 revenue figure guidance?

qa_highlights.question: Why is PM MITRA Park delayed and is there a garmenting plan?

Insurance claim (about INR27 crore inventory loss) recovery timing and deductibles; investigation expected to conclude by Q3 end.
PM MITRA Park timeline has slipped to around FY30 and capex may rise above INR300 crores; Tamil Nadu incentive eligibility for the INR410 crore project is still under discussion.

Bangladesh LDC extension and FTA benefit timing (a year out) affect export volumes; exports are only about 8% of revenue.

543923|2026-03.headline: IKIO Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to INR165 crores and FY26 revenue reached INR595 crores (+23%), with management guiding FY27 revenue growth of 20-22%.

For FY26, revenue was INR595 crores (+23%), EBITDA INR78 crores (margin about 13%) and PAT INR42 crores (margin about 7%). Non-lighting ("other business") rose to 71% of revenue in FY26 from 57% in FY25, and overseas revenue grew 53% to INR110 crores. Management said front-loaded strategic expenses are keeping margins elevated and that Home Lighting ODM sales to Signify are declining, while working capital has been hit by geopolitical disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated headcount and utilisation level?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is 2,500+ across all factories versus about 1,600 at IPO. Mature units run at about 70%+ utilisation; newer verticals run lower and should improve with volumes. Management declined to give a consolidated figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No order book; revenue visibility comes from customer planning forecasts. The ODM model means each new category is screened for feasibility, EBITDA margin and value addition before entry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall after the IPO, and will they recover to 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to onboarding fixed costs for new verticals (Automotive Lighting, Hearables, Honeywell, EMS, Energy). Margins have risen for 4-5 quarters; the target is 18-20%, with about 15% reached so far.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 CapEx and full-utilisation revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR35-36 crores of capex this year from IPO proceeds. On roughly INR300 crores of total investment at 4.5-5x asset turns, management pointed to about INR1,500 crores top line at full utilisation, as an intent rather than a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and comparison with EMS peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is elevated because of inventory built during geopolitical disruption and design changes; the company expects 2-3 quarters before normalising. Management said it owns designs and buys raw materials, which explains the gap with EMS peers that run negative working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly BOM-plus with a 2-3 month lag, except in-store lighting, which is market-priced. No annual price-reduction contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gravus Tech a move into B2C?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the Gravus acquisition (88% stake) is for B2B high-end project and export business, serving architects and designers.

543923|2026-06.headline: IKIO Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 169 crore and EBITDA rose 94% to Rs 22 crore, but gross margin fell to about 41% on war-driven component and metal costs.

EBITDA rose 94% YoY to Rs 22 crore (13% margin vs 9.4%) and PAT rose to Rs 11 crore from Rs 2 crore. Management said sequential profitability was hit by higher raw material and semiconductor costs linked to the Middle East war and by higher wages after a minimum wage revision. Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance at 18-20% and group EBITDA margin at 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall from 44-45% to 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed metal price volatility and semiconductor shortages and price spikes. It redesigned products to keep specs while avoiding shortages, and said 41% is sustainable at current raw material prices unless the war escalates.

qa_highlights.question: Was the other business QoQ dip due to seasonality or the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally the leanest quarter. YoY, Q1 FY27 Rs 124 crore matched the full Q1 FY26 base of about Rs 120 crore, and the war cost an estimated Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 40% growth in the home lighting ODM business and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New customers were added and the customer base diversified from one customer to 3-4. Management expects FY27 at around Rs 170 crore, plus or minus Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hearables and wearables production visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: H&W is about 15-16% of revenue now and is guided at 16-18% for FY27. Customers plan 3-6 months ahead, with 10-12 month pipeline discussions with larger customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of automotive lighting and the OEM path?

Full-year consolidated revenue rose about 78% to roughly INR722 crore, EBITDA about 77% and PAT about 74%, though management conceded PAT margin was about 7% versus a restated ~6% base. Installed capacity reached 133,600 MT with actual production of about 106,370 MT, and the order book stands at INR760 crore. The H1 bidder status for Amzen Transportation was described as reinstated after Supreme Court rulings, with the CoC approval and LOI still awaited.

segments.commentary: Installed capacity 65,000 MT, up from about 12,500 MT when acquired. Produced 56,380 MT in FY26; galvanizing bath running at about 24,000 MT per year, with a plan to scale to about 85,000 MT in the same space.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three reasons: weak springs profitability, about INR2-2.5 crore carrying cost of Amzen KMPs, and about INR10 crore legal and related costs on Amzen, which auditors did not allow to be capitalised. Total hit about INR8 crore to PAT.

543931|2026-06.headline: Veefin standalone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 128% YoY to Rs 23.14 crore, with EBITDA at Rs 12.83 crore (55.4% margin) and PAT at Rs 6.74 crore.
543931|2026-06.overview: Management reported standalone revenue of Rs 23.14 crore (up 128% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 12.83 crore at a 55.4% margin, and PAT of Rs 6.74 crore (up 151% YoY). Consolidated revenue was Rs 113.97 crore with PAT of Rs 9.5 crore, which management said reflects the group perimeter rather than margin deterioration. Five new clients were signed, including a six-product win with a GCC digital bank, and the qualified pipeline ended the quarter at about $80 million after $15.27 million converted. The amalgamation is at step five of seven, with the NCLT second motion petition being filed. Management also disclosed Rs 50 crore of short-term debt at roughly 14-15%, secured by promoter share pledges, to bridge working capital.

segments.name: Consolidated (statutory perimeter, incl. subsidiaries and group entities)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 113.97 crore, EBITDA Rs 22.4 crore (19.7%), PAT Rs 9.5 crore (8.3%). Management attributes the lower margin to subsidiaries' different business profile, not deterioration.

guidance_outlook: Management says FY27 is the year the platform shifts from building to monetising; amalgamation expected to close within the next quarter to quarter and a half, with NCLT final order as the last substantive step.
Revenue from signed deals to be recognised as implementation fees over roughly 9 months, then licence fees from go-live, and AMC from year 2; all five Q1 contracts are five-year terms.
Services EBITDA margin (about 20%) expected to remain similar over the next 3-5 years, per management.
Half-yearly numbers to show TREDX platform revenue, as payment milestones for signed trade and cash deals fall in later periods.
Management plans to retire the short-term debt (2-3 year tenure) earlier than maturity.
capex_capacity: Management said the capex cycle this year is much lower than last year, but working capital needs remain because revenue is lumpy while spend is roughly constant through the year.
PSB Xchange: 3 lenders live, 7 under integration (about half non-PSU), 22 yet to start; 10 lenders now presented deals (3 live plus 7 in progress).
PSB Xchange limits increased to Rs 5,800 crore from Rs 5,400 crore; cumulative requirements rose to Rs 26,000 crore; 94 corporate deals in the pipeline at some stage.
Management sees an inflection point at 10-12 integrated banks, when inter-bank competition starts.
demand_pricing: Qualified pipeline bridge: opened at $79.62 million, added $20.4 million, converted $15.27 million, and removed about $4.5 million deferred on timelines; closed at $80.13 million.

Five new clients signed in Q1, including a six-product win with a large GCC digital bank (LOS, LMS, collections, trade finance, supply chain, limits microservice) and a Middle East non-bank lender taking LOS, LMS and collections; a five-country Africa supply chain and LOS rollout.
Pipeline and deal values are stated as five-year contract value (implementation, licence and AMC fees combined).
Management says Veefin wins on technology architecture but falls short against incumbents with 30-40 year histories.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise debt at 15-16% when equity is cheaper, and why is Rs 50 crore needed if capex is falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited equity market timing, permanent dilution, and the view that the stock price is not attractive. Promoters pledged shares to secure the debt. The debt is for working capital gaps from lumpy revenue, with plans to retire it over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: Is pipeline stalling, given it moved only from Rs 79.62 crore to Rs 80.13 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $15.27 million was converted and $20.4 million added, replenishing about 25% of the opening pipeline in one quarter. It acknowledged the replenishment should ideally have been slightly lower.

qa_highlights.question: Why are only 3 of 32 lender integrations live?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed delays to lender IT bandwidth and PSU legacy systems, and said non-PSU lenders make up about half of the 7 integrations in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What triggers invocation of the promoter pledge, and what happens if the NCLT approval slips?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pledge is not price-linked. The covenants are EBITDA at most 3x and DSCR at least 1.25, with headroom described as large. Management does not expect NCLT delay; if it slips by months, it is outside company control.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Rs 60 crore subsidiary debts, and did standalone guarantee them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 60 crore sits with subsidiaries Infini and Nityo, and that Veefin (standalone) has provided guarantees for it.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PSB Xchange pipeline Rs 26,000 crore while approvals are Rs 5,800 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said banks set their own pace; the platform surfaces requests to providers but cannot accelerate bank decisions. Competition among banks is expected once 10-12 are integrated.

543931|2026-09.headline: Veefin H1 FY27 group revenue rose 116.2% to Rs 238.82 crore, with group PAT of Rs 24.85 crore and a 25.5% EBITDA margin.
543931|2026-09.overview: Group revenue for H1 FY27 was Rs 238.82 crore, up 116.2% YoY, with group EBITDA of Rs 60.81 crore (25.5% margin) and PAT of Rs 24.85 crore (10.4% margin). Q2 revenue rose 9.2% QoQ to Rs 124.66 crore, and Q2 EBITDA margin was 29.4% versus 21.1% in Q1. Management reported an open pipeline of about Rs 920 crore with Rs 240 crore added in Q2, a new AI operating system (AIOS), and senior hires in delivery and customer roles. Operating cash flow was negative in H1, which management attributed to timing of billing and collections, and it expects H2 to improve.

segments.name: Standalone revenue mix
segments.commentary: Recurring fees were 82.1% of standalone H1 revenue and 89.8% in Q2. Existing customers contributed 73.9% of H1 revenue and 69.9% of Q2 revenue.

segments.name: Opportunity pipeline by product
segments.commentary: Supply chain finance about 35% of pipeline value, digital lending about 23%, trade and cash about 18%, digital banking about 16%, and fraud and risk in single digits. Geographically, about 84% is outside India (Southeast Asia, Middle East, Africa) and 16% in India.

segments.name: Subsidiary: White Rivers Media
segments.commentary: Consolidated for six months in H1 FY27 versus three months in H1 FY26, which management cited as a reason for the rise in cost of revenue. A DRHP listing filing is expected in January.

guidance_outlook: Management stated its EBITDA margin guidance range is 45% to 50%, and it is currently tracking above that range.
Management said it would not give formal forward guidance but expects its current revenue growth rate to continue for the next two years.
Management said product development spend is at the end of its cycle, and from next year essentially 99% will flow through the P&L rather than the balance sheet.
Management said no fresh debt or equity raise is planned; only already-sanctioned working capital lines will be drawn.
H2 is expected to be stronger on billing and collections, which management expects to reverse the H1 negative operating cash flow on a full-year basis.
capex_capacity: Veefin AIOS (AI operating system) has more than 1,000 reusable skills built, and three internal factories (implementation, support and testing) are running on it.
BSE in-principle approval for migration to the main board is in place; the NSE application is pending.
Voluntary adoption of Ind AS was made in preparation for the main board move, with restatement of past financials.
PSB Xchange: dealers onboarded, anchor approvals in place, AUM building; management declined to share revenue or AUM.
Hiring: Pavan (Chief Delivery Officer, ex-Tech Mahindra) and Akash Munjal (Chief Customer Officer) joined or were moved into roles in the last quarter.
demand_pricing: Open pipeline of about Rs 920 crore at the start of Q2, with about Rs 240 crore of net new opportunities added in the quarter.
About Rs 46 crore was contracted out of the pipeline in the quarter, and about Rs 35 crore was lost to deferrals or cancellations.
77 opportunities in the pipeline, of which 38 involve more than one product. About 75% of pipeline value is fully qualified, including about 11% under negotiation.
Management said new revenue drivers are a mix of existing-client revenue, new clients, and new product lines, with no geographic expansion planned.

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of existing-client revenue over contract periods, new client wins, and new product lines; no new geographies, with India a smaller part of the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product development expenses were reduced in H1 and that H1 product development spend was Rs 56-57 crore versus Rs 65 crore a year earlier; the balance-sheet capitalisation is ending, so 99% will flow through the P&L from next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from Q1 to Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 45-50% guided range is the reference, and quarterly fluctuations are expected; the current margin is above that range.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cash in hand low and how is liquidity managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital lines have been sanctioned but not fully drawn, as bank payments are expected at any time.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Payal Maisheri said H1 cash flow lags P&L because of paying current and statutory liabilities, unbilled revenue and prepaid expenses. H2 billing is larger, and she expects the other current assets to turn positive over the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Will management share product-level metrics for PSB Xchange and other products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product-level revenue, AUM, or run-rate, citing competitive sensitivity and partner-bank requests, and said it will share company-level numbers only.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow in H1 FY27, with DSO still at 88 days and a large unbilled revenue balance that must convert in H2.

Pipeline is 84% outside India, and 65% sits outside supply chain finance; conversion of the Rs 920 crore pipeline (Rs 46 crore contracted in Q2) is the key test.
Q2 standalone and group EBITDA margins are above management's 45-50% range, and management flagged that margins will fluctuate.
Limited product-level disclosure (PSB Xchange, trade, lending) makes it hard for investors to track segment performance.
Amalgamation NCLT final hearing expected in November or December; WRM DRHP filing expected in January.
Investor queries on the FY25 fundraise were answered with Rs 160 crore (subsidiaries, Sep 2024) and Rs 88 crore (Veefin, Dec 2025) amounts, which management confirmed.

543932|2026-03.headline: ideaForge Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR141 crore with EBITDA margin of 52.6%, while FY26 PAT stayed negative at INR17 crore.
543932|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue and PAT, with about 40% of the Q3 open order book executed in the quarter. FY26 revenue rose to INR286.1 crore from INR161 crore, and EBITDA turned positive at INR27 crore for the year. Management opened FY27 with an order book of about INR310 crore, all slated for execution within roughly three quarters, and signalled a push into combat drones (loitering munitions, strike UAVs) alongside its ISR core. Guidance is limited to a blended FY27 gross margin of 50-55%.

segments.name: Civil and enterprise
segments.commentary: Smaller share of the order book; management is pursuing drone-as-a-service, analytics and enterprise software-led offerings. Power-line tower inspection is a newly addressed market.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: First US order from Lamar Police Department, Texas, as an early pilot. JV formed with FirstBreach in the US; MoU with Digital Media Professionals Inc. in Japan. Management did not quantify international revenue.

segments.name: YETI (middle-mile logistics)
segments.commentary: Still in development. Military high-altitude heavy logistics is the first target; tentative commercial exploration expected to start in FY27.

543957|2026-03.headline: RedTape FY26 revenue rose 19.6% to INR2,415 crores and EBITDA margin widened to 19% from 17.5%, with standalone PAT of INR244 crores.
543957|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year where the business absorbed a weak first half and then accelerated in Q3 and Q4, helped by the GST cut on footwear below INR2,500. Q4 revenue was INR674 crores with a 43.4% gross margin and standalone PAT of INR71 crores. Management attributed the lower reported gross margin to e-commerce rebates now netted against top-line, with other income carrying these rebates. Working capital improved: debt fell about INR200 crores from September to March and operating cash flow was stated at INR175 crores, though inventory days remain high at about 170.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: INR1,535 crores in FY26, about 63% of revenue; remains the footfall anchor, with casual and athleisure growing within it.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.commentary: INR805 crores in FY26, about 34% of revenue; management is investing most here for FY27, including women's apparel. Segment margin not disclosed.

segments.name: Accessories
segments.commentary: INR75 crores in FY26, about 3% of revenue; sunglasses, hard luggage and grooming grew faster than the other segments from a small base.

segments.name: Brands
segments.commentary: Ozark (outdoor/adventure) response exceeded expectations and store rollout is being scaled. Bond Street and Mode were launched in FY26; no figures given.

guidance_outlook: Plan to open 200-250 stores in FY27 (500-1,500 sq ft), with COCO share of 25-35% and the rest FOFO; expansion into South and West India.
Inventory target of 150 days, described as 'very near future'; management earlier said it could settle at 120-150 days.
EBITDA margin band guided at 16-19%, described as a 'new normal' rather than a peak.
No MRP increase planned for the next 3-6 months; raw-material cost volatility to be reassessed after September.
Long-term target of 65-70% of revenue from retail (offline); no multi-year revenue target given.
capex_capacity: Store count crossed 550 (223 exclusive showrooms across 161 cities at year-end per prepared remarks); about 70% of stores in North India, present in 300 cities.
Seven marketplace warehouses in India, with plans to open two more; Ludhiana warehouse opened in FY26.
Unnao warehouse expanded by about 3 lakh sq ft; remaining capex went to retail expansion. Management referenced about INR450 crores of prior capex without a FY26 breakdown.
Store economics: in the franchise (FOFO) model, the franchisee bears rent, salaries, miscellaneous costs and fixtures capex; RedTape keeps billing and top line.
demand_pricing: Channel mix: offline retail about 70% of turnover; online (e-commerce and quick commerce) about 30%, primarily via Flipkart and Myntra on a marketplace model.
Management cites RedTape as the number two footwear brand on Flipkart and Myntra; online repeat customers at 54-58%.
Pricing: no MRP hikes yet; company works on cost-plus and has about six months of POs and LCs covered.
Management said the Q4 volume lift was not only GST-driven, citing wedding season, healthy footfalls and same-store growth; SSSG was 17.8% in Q4.
Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns hold the majority of stores; consumer shift to organised branded product cited.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high (about 175 days on sales, over 300 days on COGS) and where will it settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory peaked above 250 days and is now about 170, driven by marketplace warehouse build-out and offline expansion. The target is 120-150 days, with 150 as the ideal near-term level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall while EBITDA improved, and what is the medium-term EBITDA view?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce rebates are now netted against revenue, so the gross margin decline is top-line driven, with no PBT impact. CFO said EBITDA has hovered around 16-18%, with 19% described as a new normal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other income of INR133 crores and the FY25 restatement?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR88 crores is e-commerce discounts/rebates and the rest is claims from platforms. The FY25 restatement was an accounting change, applied to the prior year as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the apparel margin and the operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not report footwear and apparel margins separately and did not give a figure. On cash flow, CFO said operating cash flow reached INR175 crores and debt fell about INR200 crores since September.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin, the COCO/FOFO split, and the accessories strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin is about 16.4%. About 25-27% of stores are COCO. Accessories expansion is framed as raising wallet share and SSSG, building on belts, wallets and caps.

qa_highlights.question: Payable days appear to have dropped sharply; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management initially deferred the question and the CFO said he would revert, citing payable days history of about 171-188 days in recent years.

risks_watch: Inventory at about 170 days versus the 150-day target; operating cash flow and short-term borrowings depend on this.
Payable days reportedly fell sharply (about 55 days per an analyst's reading); management has not yet explained this.
Raw material cost pressure; price increases are deferred until after September, and no price hikes are taken.
Gross margin optics shaped by e-commerce rebate accounting; EBITDA margin band is wide (16-19%).
Apparel margin not disclosed, and the segment is now 34% of revenue and the focus of FY27 investment.

543957|2026-06.headline: Redtape Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 19.4% YoY to INR47 crore on 3.7% revenue growth to INR480 crore, with no price hikes and e-commerce deliberately de-prioritised.

PAT rose 19.4% to INR47 crore, the company's highest-ever Q1 profit in absolute terms. Management held MRPs flat and absorbed minimum wage and input cost inflation through sourcing, supply chain and retail efficiencies. E-commerce declined as management refused to match marketplace deep discounting, and online share of revenue fell to 22% from 30%. Management described the e-commerce dip as a one-off, but gave no quantified guidance.

segments.name: Core India retail
segments.commentary: Softer early in the quarter, improved as the quarter progressed. Management credits store-led model and better product/category mix for margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: UAE franchise stores were hit early in the quarter and recovered in the last month. UK master distributor Style Label Manchester appointed; transactions started. No export revenue guidance given.

segments.name: Sprandi (new brand)
segments.commentary: Sports brand acquired in April 2026 for India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and other countries. Shoes first, then apparel. Launch in India online and retail by end-September 2026.

guidance_outlook: Store additions: 33 opened in Q1 FY27; aspiration of about 150 (150-plus) by FY27 end, versus an earlier 200-250 aspiration. Management says it will 'remain close to that number'.

Marketplaces pushed higher discounting; Redtape declined to match beyond levels it considered appropriate for the brand. Management said there is no fixed discount ceiling and that it decides event by event (for example BBD).

ASPs rose sequentially across footwear and apparel from product and category mix, not broad-based price hikes. MRPs were held flat despite minimum wage and input cost inflation linked to the ongoing war.
Management declined to quantify inflation, calling it 'a regular business'.
Non-BIS inventory remains; the industry has an extension of one year, with management expecting a further extension.
A September 2025 income tax search is ongoing; management says no material claim or risk has been identified so far.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the e-commerce weakness, and what is the discount level beyond which Redtape will not participate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was a deliberate choice, not a structural weakness. It declined to set a fixed discount threshold, saying it depends on event size and margin impact, and that it expects e-commerce to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inflation burden and will price hikes follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimum wage and war-related costs were absorbed, MRPs were not raised, and it would not quantify the inflation as it is a regular business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the lower other income?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vivek Agnihotri said lower e-commerce platform rebates cut other income to around INR8-9 crore from about INR28 crore in the prior-year quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement above 200 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said retail margins were stronger, with operating leverage and an optimised supply chain. No category-level margin split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Does Q1 margin mean moderation is likely for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the intent is to keep margins intact and aspire to improve them, while noting that it will not sacrifice margins for top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the income tax search from September 2025?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the process is ongoing and could take 2-3 years, with no material claim or risk identified to date.

543957|2026-09.headline: Redtape Q2 FY27 revenue fell 3.5% YoY to INR 474 crores on Big Billion Days shift, but EBITDA margin rose 204 bps to 18.9% and PAT grew 27.3%.

Profitability improved: gross margin rose to 45.4%, EBITDA grew 8.2% to INR 89 crores (margin 18.9%, up 204 bps), and PAT grew 27.3% to INR 36 crores. For H1, revenue was broadly flat at INR 955 crores, with EBITDA up 12.4% and PAT up 22.7%. Online share recovered to about 31% of revenue from about 22% in Q1, and the brand website sales reached INR 31.9 crores versus INR 3.9 crores a year earlier.

segments.name: Footwear and apparel
segments.commentary: Footwear accounted for 63% of Q2 revenue. Apparel and accessories are being built on shared sourcing, merchandising and distribution. No separate segment figures were given.

543959|2026-03.headline: SBFC Q4 FY26: AUM up 29% YoY to INR 11,270 crore, PAT up 30% to INR 123 crore, credit cost steady at 1.38%.
543959|2026-03.overview: SBFC reported Q4 FY26 AUM of INR 11,270 crore, up 29% YoY and 8% QoQ, with gold loans reaching 21% of the book. Spreads widened 56 bps YoY to 9.09% as cost of borrowing fell 83 bps to 8.52%, and opex fell 69 bps YoY to 3.93%. PAT rose 30% YoY to INR 123 crore, with FY26 PAT at INR 451 crore (+31%). Management kept FY27 guidance broadly unchanged: 5-7% quarterly growth, flat spreads, opex down 20-25 bps and credit cost range-bound around 1.38%. Branch count reached 251 with a plan to stabilise near 275.

segments.name: Loan against gold
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,374 crore, 21% of book, growing 63% YoY; management says growth is mainly price-driven and the share may move toward 25%. Around 220 of 251 branches are pure gold branches.

segments.commentary: Co-origination was 16% of Q4 disbursements and 18-19% of AUM, and is expected to hold similar levels through FY27.

capex_capacity: Branches: 251 at March 2026 after adding 21 in Q4 and 46 in FY26; target to stabilise at about 275 in FY27.

demand_pricing: Management said growth in gold has been mostly price-driven rather than tonnage-driven; gold prices are expected to stay range-bound or flat.
