South disbursals and AUM grew more slowly last year, which lifted the West's share of AUM (management said mix to stay similar for two quarters).
Early April data showed no new stress in sectors hit by LPG and fertilizer pressures; bounce rates marginally lower.
Management expects no increase in cost of borrowing in FY27; G-Sec volatility and a temporary liquidity squeeze were flagged.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee and branch opex per unit flat for many quarters, and how long can that continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said upfront investment in state, regional and supervisor layers is already in place, so incremental cost is mainly front-end staff at low unit cost; opex is still guided down 20-25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC need DSAs or connectors to sustain growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said the current distribution can deliver about 20% disbursal growth next year, with no need for indirect channels for at least two years.

qa_highlights.question: Sensitivity of growth and gold mix to gold prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said gold growth is mostly price-driven; FY27 gold growth is pencilled in on full-year benefit from branches added in FY26, not on higher prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost guidance conservative given early delinquency improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahesh Dayani said guidance is cautious given the macro (fuel, rainfall, heat); April numbers show no stress in LPG- and fertiliser-linked sectors.

qa_highlights.question: Path to ROE of 18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ROE is an outcome of ROA and leverage (about 4.57% ROA, 3.17x leverage, ~14.5% ROE); management called 18% optimistic and cited more than 15% ROE on 25% growth if ROA compresses about 25 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ARC sell-down a driver of reported GNPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said ARC sales are used to clean up hard-to-collect assets and recoveries under SARFAESI; benefits flow to P&L. No extra provision overlay was held beyond the March model refresh.

risks_watch: Macro shocks: oil price pass-through, weaker rupee, poor monsoon/El Nino, Gulf remittance risk, all flagged by management.
Gold price reversal would slow the gold book, which is 21% of AUM and the main driver of growth.
Credit cost guided flat at 1.38% while stage 2 rose from about 6% to 16% (per Mahesh Dayani); watch slippage and 1+ DPD (benchmarked 7-9%).
Disbursement volumes are down YoY and branches added in gold and MSME may not reach productivity targets as planned.
Rating upgrade is possible but not guided; management declined to comment.

rows.why: No new product, brand or model launch was discussed.

543959|2026-06.headline: SBFC Q1 FY27: PAT rose 29% YoY to INR 130 crores and spreads widened 39 bps QoQ to 9.48%, while 0+ DPD rose 70 bps and AUM grew 6% QoQ.
543959|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR 11,922 crores (up 27% YoY, 6% QoQ), with MSME AUM at INR 9,271 crores and gold loan AUM at INR 2,631 crores. Spreads improved to 9.48% and NIM to 10.6%, helped by a 90 bps YoY drop in cost of borrowing to 8.42%. Management cited headwinds: lower gold-loan eligibility after April 1, 2026 rules, a regulatory cap on bank collateral for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets that hit co-origination, and softer login-to-disbursal conversion (34% vs 42%). Asset quality weakened QoQ, with 0+ DPD up 70 bps and GNPA at 2.66%, but Stage 2 ECL was raised to 16% from 6% and total provisioning reached 1.91% of assets.

financial_highlights.change: up by similar bps as spread (QoQ)
Stage 2 ECL raised to 16% from 6%; about 2x regulatory minimum

segments.name: MSME / small-ticket LAP
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,271 crores (+4.5% QoQ) and disbursements INR 809 crores (+3% QoQ). Co-origination, about 20% of disbursals and book, reset to about 10% after RBI collateral rule for sub-20 lakh MSME tickets; management expects a return to usual run rate from this quarter.

segments.name: Gold loan
segments.commentary: AUM INR 2,631 crores (+11% QoQ). Gold yields rose in the quarter and were the main driver of the 29 bps QoQ yield increase; management expects gold yields to stay range-bound, with at most a marginal decline.

guidance_outlook: Opex to average AUM to fall 25 bps in FY27 (reiterated), and to be closer to 4% or below by year-end as new branches mature.
Credit cost expected at 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.
Yield expected to stabilise in the 17.50%-17.75% range; spreads to be held above 9%.
Cost of borrowing expected to stabilise at current levels after upfronting borrowings and liquidity build-up.
Branch expansion limited to 10-15 in FY27, after 5 branches added in Q1 (total 256), with further expansion tied to returns from recent branches.
Management says guidance for the coming quarter is unchanged; AUM target path to INR 15,000 crores with higher liquidity held on balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Branch count 256 as of June 2026 after adding five in Q1; roughly 52 branches opened over the last year, with the bulk in H2 FY26.
Plan for FY27 is 10-15 new branches, with expansion gated on profitability of recently opened branches.
Closing liquidity INR 1,864 crores; management intends to hold higher liquidity as it grows toward INR 15,000 crores AUM.
Capital adequacy ratio 32%; tangible net worth INR 3,613 crores.
demand_pricing: Login-to-disbursal conversion fell to 34% from 42%; management expects it to hold near 35% as higher logins and co-origination recover.
Around 1,400 applications per quarter (about 7% of roughly 21,000 logins), or about INR 140 crores of disbursals, were not passing filters; management will not push loans that fail screens.
Sub-10 lakh household segment showing leveraged stress; CIBIL scores above 700 for about 90% of the portfolio, but eligibility is the binding constraint.
Competitors pricing aggressively or offering larger loan amounts; management chose to walk away from some business to protect spreads.
Gold-loan eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026, and falling gold prices reduced the loan amount reaching customers.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the sub-10 lakh segment in its credit cycle, and how does that affect FY27 growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said conditions there have not improved and it is watchful. Aseem Dhru cited household DSR near 14% per CLSA, and said the company does not know whether it is early or mid-cycle.

qa_highlights.question: Will SBFC add new products in the next 12-18 months beyond small-ticket LAP and gold loans?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it will focus on getting better at the existing two products and sees no need for new products or geographies to meet FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Increments were rolled out, and about 20-25 branches opened in Q4 FY26 plus 5 in Q1 brought their full-year staff costs into this quarter. Cost to AUM should fall as those branches mature over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Was the 30 bps yield increase driven by higher risk-taking?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanket Agrawal said gold yields rose this quarter, adding to the yield improvement. Company yield is expected to stabilise at 17.50%-17.75%, with spreads held above 9%.

qa_highlights.question: Is credit cost stable at about 1.4% for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management expects credit cost of 1.4%-1.5% for at least the next two quarters; Q1 was 1.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for incremental yield and gold yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental yield is in the same 17.50%-17.75% range, slightly up because of gold. Gold yields are expected to be range-bound with at most a marginal fall; the recent 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated.

risks_watch: Sub-10 lakh household segment: management says conditions have not improved, CLSA household DSR near 14%, and the company cannot tell whether the cycle is early or mid; watch the disbursal mix and ticket size there.
Asset quality: 0+ DPD rose 70 bps QoQ and management called it homework for the current quarter, expecting stabilisation this quarter and rollbacks in later quarters; GNPA 2.66%.
Co-origination recovery: management expects co-origination to return to its usual run rate this quarter after the RBI collateral rule cut its share to about 10%; verify in Q2 disbursals.
Cost to AUM: opex 4.29% needs to fall to about 4% or below by year-end as branches opened in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 mature; employee cost stays elevated in the near term.
Funding and rates: management flagged an upward bias in Indian interest rates from crude above $100 and deposit rates, while saying cost of borrowing should now stabilise at current levels.
Gold yields: management says the 25-30 bps rise should not be extrapolated and gold yields may drift marginally lower; spread floor of 9% depends on holding yields at 17.50%-17.75%.
key_quotes: We'd rather over-insulate the P&L now than explain a surprise later, call it prudence with a margin of safety.
So, we don't want to, at this stage look at anything different or new.
But I think the only parameter that one should probably look at is whether we've been able to maintain our spreads.
My sense is that the 25-30 basis increase you shouldn't pencil-in and extrapolate the numbers from here.

rows.why: Eligibility norms reset from April 1, 2026 and falling gold prices reduced loan amounts reaching customers, though gold AUM still grew 11% QoQ to INR 2,631 crores and gold yields are expected to stay range-bound.

543959|2026-09.headline: SBFC Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27% YoY to INR 139 crore, with ROE at 15.04% and AUM up 27% YoY to INR 12,592 crore.
543959|2026-09.overview: SBFC reported its 36th consecutive quarter of sequential AUM and profit growth, with AUM at INR 12,592 crore (up 6% QoQ, 27% YoY) and PAT of INR 139 crore (up 7% QoQ, 27% YoY). Credit cost eased to 1.37% from 1.44% and Opex fell to 4.07%, while spreads widened to 9.63%. Management said the gold-loan delinquency rise after the RBI circular was the main source of higher Stage 2 assets, and that the MSME book has stabilised rather than improved. Management kept its 5-7% quarterly AUM growth guidance and warned against treating 9.6% spreads as a new norm.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME AUM INR 9,669 crore (77% of AUM), up 18% YoY and 4.3% QoQ; on-book grew 20% and co-origination 10%. MSME disbursements INR 855 crore, up 6% QoQ, the third straight quarter of growth.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan AUM INR 2,906 crore (about 23% of AUM); added INR 275 crore in Q2, roughly INR 40 lakh net growth per branch per month across 236 gold branches. Management is deliberately cautious on volume and LTV expansion.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 5-7% per quarter going forward; management said MSME disbursements should grow in double digits second-half over second-half.
Opex expected to fall by a further 25 bps in FY27, with a further reduction over the next two quarters.
Spread guided around 9-9.25%, but management asked investors not to model 9.6% as the norm due to rising gold competition and likely pricing rationalisation.
Credit cost seen stabilising at around 1.37% or marginally lower unless El Nino or state waivers materially change the outlook; 1.45% in Q1 described as likely peak.
Capital sufficient to an AUM of about INR 20,000 crore before the next capital raise; ROE expansion expected as leverage rises.
PLR raised 25 bps in October 2026; management expects spreads to hold as variable-rate MSME assets reprice.
CARE and India Ratings revised outlook from stable to positive.
capex_capacity: Branch count 257 as of September 2026 (1 added in Q2, 6 in H1); 236 branches do gold loans.
Collection team about 850 including supervisors (about 700 front-end), up 150-200 in the period.
LCR at 194%; closing liquidity INR 1,782 crore in Q2 versus INR 1,864 crore in Q1.
AI voice ran the first full pre-due collection cycle in October: more than 4 lakh calls to 35,000 accounts, 84% reached, 53% paid, replacing roughly a 60-person team.
demand_pricing: Banks are moving to higher-ticket prime borrowers at single-digit pricing, leaving INR 10-25 lakh and INR 25+ lakh MSME segments with headroom for SBFC.
Sub-INR 7 lakh book is being run down and is no longer originated; it is under 6% of AUM per management.
Gold competition rising as large players open branches; gold yields range 18-21%, with management expecting roughly 23% and possibly 25%.
Co-origination rose to INR 112 crore from INR 78 crore in Q1.
Management expects MSME disbursements to stabilise and grow; Q2 was the highest disbursement level in the MSME business since listing per management.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan stress and how the industry is positioned, given larger players entering gold.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not chase high-volume gold growth, as it expects pricing to be compromised; it said gold yields are 18-21% and competition has risen in the last 1-1.5 months, with some large players opening 500-1,000 branches.

qa_highlights.question: Why slippages (GS2+GS3) rose QoQ, and whether the ARC sale was gold or MSME.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise in Stage 2 is entirely from gold loans after the RBI circular reset scheme design, as customers move from bullet to monthly interest payments. The ARC sale was a lower-ticket vintage LAP portfolio; no gold loans were sold.

qa_highlights.question: Gold price sensitivity and LTV risk.
qa_highlights.answer: LTV fell to 67% from about 70% last quarter (versus about 60s in June 2025). Auctions are triggered after 85-90% LTV and delinquency, with a 7-30 day window per management; out-of-money risk described as not significant.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of MSME disbursement pick-up.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the repositioning is done and restaffing is complete in most locations; it expects second-half over second-half disbursement growth of at least double digits.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state 0+ DPD and credit cost.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 0+ rose from around 7% to above 9% and is now stabilising; it expects 0+ to hold in the 8-9.2% range, not return to 7%, and credit cost to stabilise near 1.37%.

qa_highlights.question: Whether 4.5% ROA can be sustained as guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA has held above 4.5% for 7-8 quarters despite higher leverage; holding 4.6% over the long run will be difficult, but it should hold in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: Collection headcount and bandwidth.
qa_highlights.answer: About 700 front-end collectors and 850 including supervisors; average caseload of 40-45 per collector, varying from 25-30 in Assam to about 50 in South India.

risks_watch: Gold: competitive pricing pressure, possible yield compression, and a possible fall in gold prices (LTV fell to 67%; October saw a drop).
El Nino and drought: rainfall deficit concentrated in Karnataka and Maharashtra; state-level waivers could affect repayment behaviour.
Rising rates: 25 bps repo hike and cost of funds expected to rise; management expects spreads to hold, but pass-through of MCLR-linked debt is still to come.
Draft regulatory circular that management said may affect profitability.
Stage 2 and 0+ DPD trends, with 0+ above 9% versus about 7% historically; track whether they keep stabilising in Q3.

543960|2026-03.headline: Concord Biotech FY26 revenue fell 12% to a level where API sales were INR 829 crores, with management guiding to growth slightly above its ~18% historical rate in FY27.
543960|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a difficult year: revenue declined about 12% and Q4 revenue fell 24% YoY, driven by a roughly three-month CDSCO-related halt in European supplies, a Middle East tender held in abeyance, and a US Veterans Affairs tender on hold. Management attributes the shortfall to timing rather than demand, pricing or market share loss, and says deferred volumes are spilling into FY27. 543963|2026-03.overview: Shelter Pharma reported FY26 revenue from operations of INR 73.13 Cr (up 44% YoY), EBITDA of INR 12.72 Cr (margin 17.39%, up 26% YoY) and PAT of INR 9.03 Cr (up 25% YoY). Q4 revenue was INR 39.84 Cr (up 50% YoY) and exports were about INR 6 Cr (up 164%). Management is expanding sales teams and distributors, which has compressed margins from roughly 20-21% in FY24-FY25, and working capital has stretched to 234 days with operating cash flow of minus INR 12.48 Cr. Management reiterated the INR 200 Cr FY2030 revenue target and outlined a second plant near Ahmedabad, with capex of about INR 12-15 Cr.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: About INR 6 Cr in FY26, up 164%, mainly Africa and Middle East (UAE, Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar, Nepal, Bangladesh, Mauritius, Yemen, Sudan). Management says export margins are 20-25% higher than domestic; over INR 5 Cr already reached in Q1 FY27 per management.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said advances (about INR 37 Cr per an analyst's reading) are raw-material advances for long-term procurement and export pipeline orders; no return was specified.

qa_highlights.question: Why did promoter stake fall?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it was internal structuring: a family member was exiting part of the stake, and the promoter is buying stakes; not a promoter stake sale.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East war hit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pharma is treated as essential; three shipments are in transit to Africa and one to Dubai, with no margin impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 200 Cr target conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is realistic: exports were about INR 2.5 Cr in FY25 and about INR 6.5 Cr in FY26, with over INR 5 Cr already in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the next plant and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates INR 12-15 Cr, mostly from internal accruals, with installation starting around end-2027 after approvals from December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin down from about 20% to 17%, and what is the outlook?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it moved from advance payments in three states to credit terms in new states; credit days were cut from 120 to 90 and are targeted at 60, then about one month.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was mainly for working capital to fund a sales team that is expected to double in the next two years.

543965|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record Rs 3,032 crore (+21.3% YoY) and adjusted EBITDA rose 37.5% to Rs 222 crore, with a record Rs 524 crore of new business wins.
543965|2026-03.overview: TVS SCS posted its first Rs 3,000-plus crore revenue quarter, with ISCS growing 17.5% YoY and GFS 34.8% YoY on India ocean freight volumes. Adjusted EBITDA margin widened 80 bps YoY to 7.3%, driven by the Europe turnaround in ISCS and India volume growth in GFS. Full-year revenue grew 10.1% to Rs 11,003 crore and adjusted PBT rose 166% to Rs 99.3 crore. Management guided ISCS margin to 9.5-10% and group margin to about 7.3-7.4% for FY27, with GFS rates the key swing factor. The CEO-designate's first call also marked the retirement of MD Ravi Viswanathan.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 2,283 crore (+17.5% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs 8,238.9 crore (+9.6%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% in Q4, driven by Europe recovery and steady India growth; North America scaled up a large project live in H2 FY25.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 748.8 crore (+34.8% YoY) on India ocean freight volumes; FY26 revenue Rs 2,764.1 crore (+11.4%). Margin 2.4% in Q4 on volume growth and cost actions, but freight rates remain under pressure.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected in double digits, possibly early-to-mid teens, with ISCS a strong contributor.
ISCS adjusted EBITDA margin expected at 9.5-10% in FY27, versus 9.3% in Q4 FY26.
Group adjusted EBITDA margin expected around 7.3-7.4% in FY27, dependent on GFS freight rate trajectory.
Medium term: ISCS margin of 10.5-11%; GFS margin to move toward about 5% within 4-8 quarters and settle at 6-6.5%.
Management expects PBT to grow sequentially every quarter; Swamy & Sons acquisition (completed in May 2026) expected to be margin accretive for India in FY27.
Depreciation and lease interest expected to change with a shift from long-term to short-term leases; ECL impairment expected slightly lower in FY27 than Rs 56 crore booked in FY26.
capex_capacity: Asset-light model; capital allocation prioritised to ISCS, with minimal fixed-asset investment beyond warehouses.
Lease portfolio shifting from long-term to medium and short-term rentals where operationally feasible; short-term rental charges and warehouse R&M rose in FY26.
Second site of a key North America project went live in Q4 FY26, raising Ind AS 116 depreciation to Rs 108 crore in Q4.
Swamy & Sons 3PL acquisition (FMCG and consumption supply chains in India) completed in May 2026.
Patent accepted for unified logistics platform; AI and robotics deployed in operations.
Credit rating India AA.
demand_pricing: Q4 new business wins were Rs 523.7 crore, an all-time quarterly high (21% of Q4 FY25 revenue); FY26 new business Rs 1,206.7 crore (12.1% of FY25 revenue).
Order pipeline Rs 6,100 crore; typical conversion around 22%, with a target of 23-25%.
Fortune 500 active customers rose to 100 from 91, with 9 added in FY26.
Average customer contract length: about 4-4.1 years in India, 5+ years in North America, about 7.5 years in Europe.
GFS: freight rates under pressure; management says volumes are more resilient than pricing, which is volatile due to West Asia disruptions. Company says none of its lanes are in West Asia.
North America growing at about 28.3% CAGR over five years, focused on industrial and auto accounts, with a goal of $50-60 million per large customer over 3-4 years.
Sectors with momentum include power (alternate energy), aerospace and defence (MOU with ALA), and China-plus-one relocations, which are still early.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ISCS growth, potentially 18-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the pipeline supports it if conversion rises from about 22% to 23-25%. It set expectations at double-digit, early-to-mid-teens growth, and aspires to get closer to 18%.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins should be expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: ISCS 9.5-10% from 9.3% in Q4; group about 7.3-7.4%, with GFS freight rates the main variable and management cautious on GFS.

qa_highlights.question: Why was part of the labour-code provision taken in Q4 rather than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: A Labour Ministry clarification on 16 March came after Q3 results, requiring a reassessment and a Rs 5.2 crore additional provision in Q4. The company says the clarifications are now fully provided for.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impairment loss on financial instruments of about Rs 17.6 crore, and what is the FY27 trend?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an expected credit loss provision on customers, Rs 56 crore booked in FY26. Management expects the rate to be slightly lower in FY27, as most customers are highly rated B2B.

qa_highlights.question: Is the China-plus-one opportunity material?
qa_highlights.answer: Early traction with existing customers, including an earthmoving equipment company, but deals are not yet deep. Management is waiting to see whether US buyers accelerate expansion in India.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term targets for GFS and group revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not endorse a Rs 15,000 crore target by FY29-30; its long-term aspiration is early-teens EBITDA margins, with the GFS margin reaching 6-6.5%, the leader deferring to the incoming CEO.

risks_watch: GFS freight rate volatility from West Asia disruptions; management says volumes are resilient but pricing is volatile.
Ability to lift the pipeline conversion rate from about 22% to 23-25%.
Sustaining the Europe recovery and the North America project ramp.
Labour code provisions still have grey areas and interpretation risk.

Lease cost trend and rising short-term rental and R&M costs in warehousing.

543965|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 3,335.2 crore and adjusted EBITDA rose 34% to Rs 232.2 crore, but ISCS margin fell to 8.1%.

ISCS margin slipped to 8.1% from 9.3% in Q4 on onboarding costs for new contracts and no Q4-style price corrections, while GFS margin rose to 4.1%. New business wins of Rs 543 crore were an all-time quarterly high and the pipeline reached over Rs 7,500 crore.

segments.name: ISCS (Integrated Supply Chain Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,417 crore (+21.9% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA Rs 196.3 crore at 8.1% margin, down from 9.3% in Q4 FY26 due to implementation costs on new contracts. Management targets a return to above 9% in Q2.

segments.name: GFS (Global Forwarding Solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 918 crore (+50.6% YoY), driven by ocean freight volumes in India and higher freight rates. Adjusted EBITDA Rs 38 crore at 4.1% margin, versus 2.1% a year ago; management said it wants at least 5% over time.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration of mid-teen percentage revenue growth for FY27; management expects profit to grow faster than revenue.
Target of about 4% PBT margin; management called FY27 an aspiration and said FY28 will definitely reach 4%.
ISCS EBITDA margin expected to return to about 9% in Q2 FY27 and reach 9.5% to 10% by Q4 FY27.
GFS EBITDA margin expected at 4.5% to 5%, with management wanting at least 5%.
Early-teens EBITDA margin target referenced by an analyst; management said first 45 days of Q2 are on similar lines to Q1.
ALA JV expected to contribute revenue in H2 FY27, targeting about Rs 2,000 crore in year 5 of operations; H2 expected to be stronger than H1.
capex_capacity: Warehousing footprint about 25 million sq ft per analyst; utilisation around 85%, with room to improve through racking and automation investment.

Joint venture with ALA Group for defence and aerospace: warehouse finalised, staff being trained in Italy, and warehouse certification pending before business can start in India.
Oracle ERP implemented for the India ISCS business.
demand_pricing: New business wins of Rs 543 crore in Q1 (Rs 524 crore in Q4); about two-thirds from existing customers and one-third from new logos.
Order pipeline above Rs 7,500 crore, up from Rs 6,100 crore; management expects 20-25% conversion over 12-18 months, in line with track record.
Fuel and freight cost increases are passed through to customers under contracts with some time lag; container and air cost increases also passed on.
Management expects ISCS steady-state EBITDA margin of about 8.5-9% on new contracts.
India geography revenue grew 44% YoY on record new business wins and freight volumes.
Management sees recession and geopolitical disruption as the main risk, but said it has not yet seen this playing out in customer volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ISCS EBITDA margin decline despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited transition and implementation costs on new contracts onboarded in Q4 and Q1, plus the absence of the Q4 customer price corrections. Management called it a one-time effect and expects margins to recover.

qa_highlights.question: How long do new ISCS contracts take to reach stable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 to 2 quarters, depending on the contract: about 2 quarters for implant and sub-assembly work and about 1 quarter for aftermarket or finished-goods work.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GFS margin improvement due to one-offs linked to the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth came from new wins and cost optimisation through vendor consolidation, and it expects margins to stay around current levels with high double-digit growth ahead.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ALA JV revenue potential and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to about Rs 2,000 crore revenue in year 5, with first revenue in H2 FY27. It expects the JV to be margin accretive given high entry barriers and a regulated sector.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FIT 3PL merger going ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FIT 3PL will remain a separate legal entity due to GST mechanisms for certain FMCG customers. It said the entity was never part of the announced merger.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Middle East and Africa be entered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in discussions with Middle East companies and prefers a partnership route. It said it will announce once something crystallises and is taking extra precautions due to the war.

Manpower availability across geographies.
Warehouse depreciation and lease costs rising with new space (other expenses up on short-term rentals).

543969|2026-03.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14% YoY to ₹196 crore and PAT rose 52%, with EBITDA up 68% to ₹20 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.6%.
543969|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹196 crore (+14% YoY) and FY26 revenue of ₹684 crore (+15%), with Q4 gross profit up 33% to ₹56 crore and EBITDA up 68% to ₹20 crore. FY26 PAT was ₹29 crore (4.2% margin) and EBITDA margin improved to 8.6% from 7.9%. Installed capacity rose 22% YoY to 76,931 MTPA after the major expansion phase, with utilisation around 69% in the quarter. Management said the major capex cycle is largely complete, with only about ₹20 crore of maintenance and balance capex planned for FY27. Q4 gains were helped by inventory bought at lower prices before a sharp rise in raw material costs.

segments.name: HDPE Drums

segments.name: IBC

Recycling plant (5,000 MTPA) expected to meet 10-12% of raw metal needs, with licence expected June-July 2026 and annual savings of at least ₹5 crore.
Employee cost expected to stay at about ₹7-7.25 crore per quarter.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity up 22% YoY to 76,931 MTPA; utilisation about 69% in Q4, targeted to reach about 80% in FY27.

WADA plant fully operational across IBC, HDPE and MS drums; phase 1 revenue potential about ₹200 crore, with phase 2 infrastructure built for up to ₹400 crore by adding machines.

Recycling plant processed about 200 MT in the quarter during trial; awaiting final PCB licence expected June-July 2026. Capex about ₹10-12 crore.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as fine and said price increases are being passed through, with transport cost pass-through taking 15-20 days to a month.
Raw material prices rose about ₹50 per kg; management said inventory held before the increase generated gains that will flow into Q1 FY27.
Inventory days cut to about 25-30 days from about 45 days because imports stopped and material is now bought locally; HDPE rate around ₹150-160/kg.
Management cited about 40% domestic IBC market share and said quality and technology act as entry barriers.
Management expects the FY27 product mix to be about 45% IBC, 45% polymer drums and 10-12% MS drums.

qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gains fell in Q4 and will show up in Q1. Inventory has been cut to 25-30 days because imports have stopped; conversion cost rose to about ₹25/kg from ₹20/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and repayment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Term loan repayment has started and debt is expected to be repaid over 3-4 years. Short-term borrowing rose to ₹8-10 crore, mainly due to local purchases replacing imports.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IBC and polymer segment mix change, and what are the utilisation peaks?
qa_highlights.answer: IBC and polymer drum utilisation are expected to reach 70-75% within 3-6 months. IBC is 41% of FY26 revenue versus 34% last year and is not expected to jump to 60-70%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recycling plant's potential?

543969|2026-06.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 10% and capacity utilisation only 62%.
543969|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 36% YoY to ₹222 crore, driven mainly by price pass-through of raw material increases, while volumes were 1,292 MT against 20,936 MT per quarter installed capacity (about 62% utilisation). Gross margin compressed to 23% and EBITDA grew 50% YoY at about 10% margin; PAT rose 32% YoY to ₹10.5 crore at about 5% margin. Management said EBITDA per ton was ₹16,380 versus ₹11,252 a year earlier and ₹15,053 in Q4 FY26, but also said the figure reflects a temporary price spike that is expected to normalise. Management announced a ₹20-25 crore Kutch (IBC) plant due by March 2027 and government subsidy approvals of about ₹24.9 crore (WADA) and ₹10.5 crore (Bharuch unit 7) over 10 years.

543969|2026-09.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q2 FY27 revenue up 48% YoY to Rs 238 crore, EBITDA up 61% to Rs 20.3 crore, with EBITDA/ton at Rs 13,718.
543969|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was a volume-recovery quarter: volume rose 21% YoY and 14% QoQ to about 14,798 MT, with capacity utilisation near 70% against 62% in Q1 FY27. Average realisation rose about 22% YoY to about Rs 1.61 lakh per ton, and management stressed EBITDA per ton (up 33% YoY) over margin. EBITDA margin was 8.5% versus 7.8% a year ago, and PAT margin about 4%. H1 revenue rose 42% YoY, while H1 EBITDA margin was about 9%, and management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 15% revenue growth and 11-12% EBITDA margin, including about 1.5 points from subsidy. Capex is cut to about Rs 20-25 crore in FY27 from about Rs 90 crore in FY26.

segments.name: MS drums

segments.commentary: Commissioned October 2025 (investment Rs 8-10 crore); generated Rs 33 lakh EBITDA in Q2 FY27 and is guided to about Rs 2 crore EBITDA in FY27.

segments.commentary: Commercial production started October 2025 with about Rs 70 lakh revenue in its first month.

H1 EBITDA about Rs 41 crore; management expects about Rs 45 crore in H2 FY27.
Utilisation target about 80% for FY27 (later framed as 75-80%); Kutch facility of about 10,000 IBCs per month to be commissioned by March 2027 at Rs 20-25 crore.
WADA and BHARUCH subsidies total about Rs 35 crore (WADA Rs 24.9 crore over 10 years; BHARUCH Rs 10.5 crore); management cited about Rs 3-4 crore a year hitting the bottom line.
Remaining 1 MW solar expected to start benefit next month; FY27 capex about Rs 20-25 crore versus about Rs 90 crore in FY26.

WADA facility running across SDP drums, IBCs and MS drums; WADA capacity expansion to take about 6 months and to start after March 2027 (subsidy-linked).

demand_pricing: Management says demand and volumes are rising quarter on quarter and in the current month; over 500 customers, top customer about 6% of revenue, top 10 about 29%.

Q2 revenue bridge: realisation contributed about Rs 43.6 crore, volume and product mix about Rs 24.9 crore, and trading income about Rs 8.7 crore of the Rs 77 crore increase.

Other expenses rose to about Rs 19/kg from Rs 17/kg, which management attributed to long-distance transport for pan-India customers, labour changes, and staff returning to full strength after holidays.
Raw material sourcing now about 80% local after Hormuz-related import halt.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Blended EBITDA margin 23.04% in Q1 (up 468 bps YoY but down 80 bps QoQ) with 25% target 'in next few years'; margin should recover as Taloja/Chakan manpower ramps and bellows reaches optimum, but no quarterly guidance was given and West Asia logistics costs are a drag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Flexible hose capacity 17.5 to 20 mn m/yr and SFN skid capacity 9,000 to 15,000 units/yr are under construction with budgeted capex of INR54 cr and INR48 cr, both guided for completion by start of Q3 FY27, though skid timing depends on machine vendor delays.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Hose utilisation is 65-66% and skid exit utilisation guided at 60-65% on 15,000 units (~750 skids/month) in Q4 FY27; Q1 revenue grew 72.4% YoY with flexible hoses +41% and exports +43%, but Q4 plan depends on Q3 visibility.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: after FY27 year-end, on Hyd-Air plan finalisation
rows.why: Hyd-Air capex plan for FY27 is under discussion and will be announced once finalised; hose and skid capex (INR54 cr and INR48 cr) is already committed, and utilisation at 65-66% does not yet force a new capex round.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management did not raise any numeric guidance, declined to quantify SFN share or skid margins and redirected quarterly questions to YoY/annual views; the 25% margin target was only 'held'.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Skid expansion depends on machine supplier delays (commissioning Oct-Nov, some machines arriving Q2 and Q3), the Q4 60-65% utilisation is only 'intact' pending Q3 visibility, and QoQ margin fell 80 bps on ramp-up manpower and West Asia logistics costs.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Fire-hose assembly for the largest US data-centre customer, at 23-26% margin, is expected to be commercialised by end-Q1 FY28 with international supply; realisation size not quantified.

rows.label: SFN skid demand at ~60-65% Q4 utilisation
rows.why: Q1 SFN revenue INR32.4 cr on 1,040 units (~23% of revenue); Q4 exit guided at ~750 skids/month on 15,000 capacity, 'intact' but dependent on Q3 visibility.

rows.label: Export and European data-centre hose assemblies
rows.why: Exports grew 43% YoY with Europe (Italy, Spain, France, UK) and US growing, including hose assemblies for European data-centre applications; not quantified in INR.

rows.label: Logistics cost relief from West Asia crisis
rows.why: Logistics costs rose sharply from mid-March and worsened through Q1 with no relief timing given, so it remains a margin headwind.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, scale-up and the 25% blended margin target over several years, but evasive on specifics such as skid margins, SFN revenue share, Q2 schedules and the size of the fire-hose opportunity; analysts pushed on the QoQ margin dip and the per-skid price decline.

543972|2026-09.headline: Aeroflex Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR200 crores for the first time, with total income of INR207.68 crores, up 87% YoY, and PAT of INR36.56 crores.
543972|2026-09.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 total income of INR207.68 crores (up 87% YoY), EBITDA of INR50.34 crores (up 94%, margin 24.27%) and PAT of INR36.56 crores (up 157%, margin 17.6%). H1 FY27 total income was INR353.66 crores (up 81%), with H1 EBITDA of INR83.83 crores and PAT of INR55.35 crores, already close to full-year FY26 performance. The company changed depreciation from WDV to SLM from 1 April 2026, reducing depreciation by INR8.41 crores in both Q2 and H1. It also announced a total capex of INR202 crores for capacity expansion and the merger of wholly owned subsidiary Hyd-Air Engineering into Aeroflex.

financial_highlights.metric: Depreciation impact of WDV to SLM change
financial_highlights.value: INR8.41 crores lower in Q2 and in H1
Q2 INR6 crores; Q1 INR3 crores; H1 INR9 crores
financial_highlights.change: Q2 vs INR3 crores in prior quarter

segments.name: Metal flexible hoses
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue up 40% YoY, supported by end-user industries and international customers. Current SS hose capacity utilisation is about 80%.

segments.name: Assemblies and other value-added products
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue up 44% YoY, reflecting demand for high-precision engineered flow solutions.

segments.name: Liquid cooling (skid assemblies)
segments.commentary: Contributed 24% of H1 FY27 revenue; management cited skids at upwards of 30% of total revenue. Average realisation per skid was INR3.39 lakhs in Q2. FY27 skid revenue target raised to INR150-200 crores from an initial INR125 crores.

segments.name: Vertical mix
segments.commentary: Data center is now the largest vertical. Ports and terminals is the next growth area, followed by oil and gas and steel. Combined, these verticals are about 26-27% of business, and firefighting plus steel, oil and gas about 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 total sales growth of about 60%, with revenue of INR715-725 crores at least.
Skid utilisation expected to reach 40-50% in FY27. Skid capacity is 15,000 units per annum (12,000 commissioned); expansion to 30,000 units per annum by March 2028.
SS hose capacity to rise from 20 million to 30 million meters per annum by March 2028; peak hose-assembly revenue estimated at INR850-900 crores, assuming 70-75% of capacity for assemblies.
Incremental capacity expected to generate INR500-550 crores of revenue per year at peak utilisation; peak utilisation expected in FY30.
FY30 top line guided at about INR1,500 crores versus earlier FY29 target of INR1,000 crores, with EBITDA margins of about 25% and slightly upward.
Hyd-Air merger expected to add at least a couple of percentage points to margins through cost savings; no quantified figure yet. Hyd-Air turnover is about 3% of quarterly Aeroflex turnover.
capex_capacity: Total capex of INR202 crores: INR124 crores for SS flexible flow capacity (brownfield at Taloja plus a proposed new hose-assembly facility) and INR78 crores for skids.
SS flexible flow capacity: 20 million meters per annum completed; further 10 million meters per annum to reach 30 million, due by March 2028.
Skid capacity: 15,000 units per annum expansion due December 2026, with 12,000 units already commissioned; further expansion to 30,000 units by March 2028.
Funding: internal accruals first, then bridge and long-term debt; equity raise only if needed.
Welding automation: two lines added to reduce manual work, raise capacity and reduce rejections. Patent granted for automated 3D CAD model generation of braided hose assemblies.
demand_pricing: Liquid cooling: exclusive arrangement with one large US multinational for the Indian market; no direct bidding to data center end-users. Global liquid cooling market is about $4-5 billion, growing more than 30% YoY; Vertiv is the largest player globally and in India. Indian market size not disclosed.
Visibility: confirmed pipeline of about 3 months (frozen for the current and start of next quarter); longer-term view is an estimate only.

International: advanced-stage sampling and pricing with the same customer, with no timeline given; other international prospects are at an early stage. Realisation expected to be higher than India, not quantified.
Freight and forwarding costs rose significantly on international shipping cost increases. There was no Q1-to-Q2 revenue shift.

qa_highlights.question: Expected cost savings and margin expansion from the Hyd-Air merger?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific number yet; management expects at least a couple of percentage points of margin gain from cost savings, with exact figures after the merger completes.

qa_highlights.question: Is incremental capacity exclusive to the Indian customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Exclusivity for India remains. Capacity is earmarked for customers irrespective of plant, and the remaining capacity is fungible for exports or other customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the skid utilisation outlook for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is expected to reach 40-50% of total skid capacity in FY27, with projections revised monthly or quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY30 and margin targets after the expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line of about INR1,500 crores by FY30, with EBITDA margin of about 25% and slightly upward, balancing scale benefits against pricing pressure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and skid outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 sales growth of about 60% (INR715-725 crores at least); skid revenue of INR150-200 crores against the initial INR125 crores target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables grew more slowly than sales, and trade receivable days fell in Q2 and H1 versus last year.

risks_watch: International liquid cooling supply has no timeline; audits, controls and design differences for each country may delay conversion.
Freight and shipping costs have risen sharply and are a major expense driver.
Pricing pressure as the company scales in verticals, which management cites as offsetting scale benefits.
Capex of INR202 crores relies on internal accruals and bridge debt, with equity raise possible if needed.
Skid realisation per unit varies widely (INR1.5 lakhs to INR5 lakhs), so the quarterly average is not a reliable trend.
Management declined to give details on a potential acquisition for products adjacent to SFN, and on the parent company's sanitary valves acquisition.

Management often gave ranges and said figures would follow later.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report that our best ever results with quarterly revenue crossing INR200 crores milestone for the first time ever.
So, the design actually is completely different.
We expect the realization to be definitely higher than the India market, but it will be too early for me to comment on that.

543977|2026-03.headline: Rishabh Instruments FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 161% to INR1,264 mn (16.3% margin); 20% dividend declared and FY27 EEI growth guided at 20-25%.
543977|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7.6% to INR7,751 mn in FY26 and 9.3% to INR2,049 mn in Q4, while consolidated EBITDA more than doubled to INR1,264 mn and PAT rose 292% to INR823 mn. Standalone gross margin expanded to 54% from 48.6%, driven by product mix and sourcing. Lumel Alucast (HPDC) turned adjusted EBITDA positive at INR33 mn from a loss of INR150 mn, but its revenue fell 9.6% as loss-making contracts were exited. Management declared a 20% dividend (INR2 per INR10 share) and reported net cash of INR1,276 mn.

segments.name: Standalone Rishabh Instruments
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR788 mn (+15.2% YoY) with EBITDA INR161 mn (20.4% margin); FY26 PAT INR417 mn (+78.2%). US business grew about 50% to roughly USD3 mn, with a 40-50% growth target for FY27.

segments.name: Lumel SA (Poland, electronics)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR585 mn (+35.9% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA INR167 mn (28.6% margin); FY26 PAT INR419 mn (+19.5%). A new SMT line was commissioned, 40% funded by EU funds.

segments.name: Lumel Alucast (HPDC, Poland)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR575 mn (-22.8% YoY) with Q4 PAT loss of INR58 mn; FY26 PAT loss INR41 mn vs INR252 mn in FY25. Management targets no losses in FY27 and double-digit margins in FY28.

segments.name: Smaller entities (Shanghai V&A, Sifam Tinsley US and UK)
segments.commentary: Growth of 53% (US), 25% (UK) and 23% (China) on top line; together they are 13% of the EEI business and all three are EBITDA positive.

segments.name: Solar inverters (within EEI)
segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO launched in H2 FY25 and now operationally profitable; FY27 target about INR24-25 crore, roughly double FY26.

guidance_outlook: EEI segment FY27 top-line growth guided at 20-25% (around 20-22% in the blended view), with EBITDA margin guided at 20-22%; management said margin could be higher.
Solar inverter sales target about INR24-25 crore in FY27; the new building can scale to about INR100 crore with incremental capex.
US business targeted at 40-50% growth in FY27 with a longer-term aim of about INR100 crore in 3-4 years.
Lumel Alucast FY27 revenue expected to be flat to slightly down, roughly INR180 crore in euro terms, with no losses; double-digit margin expected in FY28.
Asked about FY28 (March 2028), management said INR1,000 crore revenue may be close but not guaranteed, with EBITDA around INR200 crore if guidelines hold; for FY27 it cited INR150-160 crore EBITDA.
capex_capacity: Nashik expansion capex complete; two manufacturing facilities almost ready and under commissioning, expected to effectively double production capacity. Commissioning expected by June-July 2026.
Current transformer capacity being expanded from 6,000 to 10,000 units per day with additional lines, equipment and manpower.
Lumel SA commissioned an advanced SMT electronics assembly line in FY26, 40% funded by EU funds.
New building: one full floor dedicated to solar manufacturing, with assembly lines added as volume grows.
Medium-voltage CTs, PTs and VTs: 4-5 new products expected by end FY27, with sales from FY28; no plans for high-voltage products.
demand_pricing: Management expects Europe to be subdued, with US, Southeast Asia and Africa seeing rising power and automation investment.
Solar: Chinese SKD-based competitors are cheaper; management says about half of the product range is now cost-competitive. Europe solar is declining, so Middle East is the preferred next market.
Alucast: qualification cycles are long (volume arrives about one year after order booking); European HPDC competitors are closing and some business is shifting to India and China.
Pricing: management said it passes on material and cost increases in EEI because it owns its brands and prices.
Data centre and sectoral marketing (Sify repeat projects, UK and Ireland): the company is bundling products with software and hiring specification specialists.

qa_highlights.question: What growth and margin should be expected for the EEI business in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 20-25% top-line growth (about 20-22% blended) and 20-22% EBITDA margin; Rishabh and Lumel are each expected to grow about 20%, with smaller entities around 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Alucast's FY27 margin guidance unchanged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is a transition year with no losses and no big margin targets; double-digit margin is expected in FY28, not FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will Alucast be demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no decision has been taken; a demerger is a possibility, but nothing is concrete and the company will inform the market at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: Is solar inverter cost-competitive with Chinese products, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is close but not yet fully competitive, with about half of the range competitive. FY27 target is INR24-25 crore, with OEM supply to assemblers and own-brand sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US revenue and the long-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue reached about USD3 mn in FY26 (from USD2 mn), with 40-50% growth planned for FY27 and about INR100 crore targeted in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cross INR1,000 crore revenue and INR200 crore EBITDA by March 2028?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is possible if guidelines hold but would not commit; the EEI business at INR560 crore growing 20% would reach about INR670 crore, while Alucast stays flat.

risks_watch: Alucast volume recovery: FY27 revenue could fall below INR200 crore (about INR180 crore in euro terms); breakeven depends on winning new projects and their qualification timelines.
Solar inverter profitability: management said margins are 15-20% gross, and cost competitiveness vs Chinese imports is incomplete.
Geopolitical and energy risk: management flagged West Asia war, oil shortages and tariffs as risks to FY27 guidance; rupee depreciation affects euro-based Lumel and Alucast figures.
Timing of the Nashik capacity commissioning (June-July 2026) and the medium-voltage product launches expected by end FY27.
Dividend sustainability: 20% dividend (INR2 per INR10 share) declared; an analyst asked about future payouts of 20% or more.

543977|2026-06.headline: Rishabh Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 4.2% to INR1,983 mn, with EBITDA up 17.3% to INR333 mn at a 16.8% margin.
543977|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR1,983 mn (+4.2% YoY) and EBITDA INR333 mn (+17.3% YoY, 16.8% margin), after a INR20 mn ESOP/SAR charge; reported PAT was INR194 mn (-1.4% YoY) due to a INR20 mn rise in depreciation. The EEI segment was the engine: management cited 34% revenue growth and roughly 24% EBITDA margin, ahead of its ~20% top-line and 20-22% EBITDA guidance. Lumel Alucast remained a planned revenue decline (-41.2%) and was at operating breakeven with adjusted EBITDA of -6.4%. The company stayed net debt-free with net cash of INR1,606 mn.

segments.name: EEI (Electrical & Electronics Instrumentation)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 34% YoY with EBITDA margin around 24%, above the 20-22% guidance; management calls it the group's primary growth and profitability engine.

segments.name: Rishabh India (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR776 mn (+25.6%), EBITDA margin 22.9%; growth attributed to current transformers, data centres, solar and exports. Solar is under 5% of total and was about INR8-9 crore last year.

segments.name: Lumel S.A. (Poland)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR639 mn (+39%), adjusted EBITDA INR153 mn (24%), contributing about 50% of consolidated bottom line; one German grid-upgrade customer is roughly 20-25% of its sales.

segments.name: Lumel Alucast (HPDC)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR443 mn (-41.2%) as a planned decline; adjusted EBITDA -INR28 mn (-6.4%), at operating breakeven. Management targets adjusted EBITDA breakeven by end FY27 and double-digit margin over the medium term.

segments.name: US / UK / China and other international
segments.commentary: US and UK grew over 40% YoY and China 20.3%; US is about INR30 crore last year with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years on an organic basis. Management says these remain on a small base.

segments.name: Solar inverters
segments.commentary: Single-phase iUNO (up to 5 kW) reached operational profitability; 3-phase iNEO launched up to 12 kW this quarter, with up to 50 kW due by end FY27 and hybrid inverters in development. FY27 solar target is INR24-25 crore, rising to INR250-300 crore next year per management.

guidance_outlook: EEI guidance held at about 20% top-line growth and 20-22% EBITDA margin for the full year; management said it will try to beat this but did not raise it.
Lumel Alucast expected to reach adjusted EBITDA breakeven for full-year FY27; management sees a path to double-digit EBITDA margin in about 2 years.
US organic revenue target INR45 crore this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years.
Nashik plant to be fully finished in about 1-2 months; management targets more than 2.5x production over the next 4-5 years.
Mumbai and Delhi TMI Experience Centres to be operational by end of FY27; ~15 new products launched over two years with more than 15 planned for FY27.
CT capacity to rise from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day, with medium-voltage CTs to follow.
capex_capacity: New Nashik manufacturing facility partially commissioned; both buildings complete, with full completion expected in about 1-2 months.
Current transformer capacity being raised from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-10,000 low-voltage units per day (near-doubling), with added machinery already ordered.
Three SMT lines in PCB/EMS operations; latest is high-end and an older line is being upgraded. A fourth line will be added once the three run on three shifts.
Dedicated automated floor for solar inverter manufacturing in the new facility.
Lumel Alucast capacity is underutilised; management is filling it with higher-value orders.
demand_pricing: Domestic order bookings in Q1 were about 20% above last year, but billing lagged, leaving a backlog to be worked off.
Data-centre wins: first win announced, then 3-4 more; about 10 more quotes outstanding.

Lumel S.A. growth comes from product spread, German grid upgrades (EUR5 mn order executed; EUR3 mn follow-on running to year-end) and radiation-detection gates, with Poland security demand after the Russia-Ukraine conflict.
Lumel Alucast: RFQs in advanced stages of commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management is prioritising value over volume.
Solar inverter pricing is competitive with Chinese imports; EPC contractors are moving away from Chinese-sourced units over after-sales and warranty concerns.
Contribution margin is about 45% on average; solar and EMS run at 15-20%, while other products run at 40-75%.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the 34% EEI growth, versus the 20-25% guidance, and is there lumpiness that will moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is spread across Rishabh India (current transformers, data centres, solar), Lumel S.A. (product spread, German grid upgrades) and new products, not one lumpy item. It reiterated EEI guidance of around 20% top-line and 20-22% EBITDA margin, saying it will try to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: How fast can the US business scale, and are there inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: US revenue went from about INR20 crore to INR30 crore last year, with INR45 crore targeted this year and INR100 crore in 2-3 years organically. Actions include more sales staff, Mexico/Canada focus, UL/ANSI product redesigns, and a couple of inorganic opportunities under review.

qa_highlights.question: Lumel Alucast: what is the pipeline for returning to INR180-230 crore revenue and double-digit margins?
qa_highlights.answer: RFQs are in advanced commercial negotiation and customer approval; ramp-up takes about 6 months after award. Management sees double-digit EBITDA margin in about 2 years and says costs have been cut substantially.

qa_highlights.question: Will the quarterly EEI growth trajectory continue, and what about AI/data-centre traction in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is almost comparable to last year's Q4 and the company wants to beat guidance rather than raise it, citing seasonality in Europe and Diwali. 543978|2026-03.headline: Ratnaveer guides FY27 top line of ~1,350-1,500 crore and FY28 consolidated 2,500 crore incl. 750 crore from new CCL plant; FY26 standalone OCF negative ~48 crore.

FY26 top line was 1,078 crore against a 1,350 crore target for the current year, with stainless/fastener business guided at about 25% CAGR. Receivables rose sharply (analyst cited about 65 crore to 175 crore), which management attributed to new product launches and longer credit to new customers.

Rate growth was soft because international guests, who pay a 10-20% premium, declined; management expects rate to recover in H2 as the mix rebalances.
Upscale and upper upscale hotels earn about 4x the revenue per key of midscale hotels on a same-store basis in FY26.
GST change from 12% with input tax credit to 5% without it cost about Rs 9.2 crore in Q1 and hits midscale rooms priced below Rs 7,500 more than upscale.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna (Ambit): Why acquire the Itmenaan estate given weak revenue history, how is Leisure capital allocation growing, and what RARE opportunities are being evaluated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hotel was idle for about a year and a half after owners moved to Canada and was delisted from RARE; it expects relisting and repricing toward Rs 20,000-40,000 rates in Kumaon. Total RARE capital is about Rs 47 crore, about Rs 60 crore with Itmenaan, and leisure should stay near 10% of capital allocation.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Khanna: How much of FY27 growth is rate versus occupancy, and has July shown a sharp recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy drives growth in the first six months, with rate recovering in H2 as domestic mix rebalances from 82% toward a higher-premium international mix. July is 'trending far ahead' of Q1 exit, with rate growth now visible, but management declined to give numbers and cautioned one month is not representative.

qa_highlights.question: Jinesh Joshi (PL Capital): Are RARE sign-ups to the Marriott Outdoor Collection program on track, and why must the Rs 750 crore enabling resolution be taken now?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 of 75 RARE hotels have agreed to join; management said sign-ups are ahead of its expectations and the pace is the issue, with 10-12 hotels on rival platforms. On the resolution, management said it will be taken every year so the Board can act in time; no specific deal is identified.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja (Antique): Is the ADR slowdown (about 2.6-2.7% growth) due to West Asia disruption and Marriott-led inventory, and is occupancy at about 79% a tactical rate trade-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rate is soft because inbound international travel fell, and it focuses on same-store total revenue growth of about 9%-9.5%, within the 9%-11% long-term range. In July, total revenue growth split about half rate and half occupancy.

qa_highlights.question: Vikas Ahuja: Why an equity-linked enabling resolution rather than debt, given the investment surplus discussed at the Analyst Day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the resolution is a general enabling step to respond to unknown problems or opportunities and keep the balance sheet strong. It added that the Rs 1,200 crore to Rs 3,000 crore revenue path has no assumed acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: Shrinjana Mittal (MS Capital): Is upper upscale underperforming midscale because of downtrading, and why is GST drag above 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw ARR growth was about 3.5%-4% across segments, and midscale RevPAR grew 13.7% at 81.3% occupancy versus 78.4% for upper upscale. GST drag is larger in Q1 and Q2 from volume sales below Rs 7,500, is lower in H2, and is about 2% per management.

qa_highlights.question: Vaibhav Muley (Haitong): Why did F&B growth slow to about 4%, and what is the GIC partnership scope?
qa_highlights.answer: F&B grew about 3.5%-4% against room revenue growth of 14%, due to a shift to domestic guests (80%-83%), a Bangalore restaurant renovation, and West Asia-related event cancellations moved to July-August. GIC has a right to 35% of new upscale deals post-JV, with no talks on existing assets; Navi Mumbai and W Hyderabad are 100% SAMHI-owned.

qa_highlights.question: Prashant Biyani (Elara): Timing for Grand Hyatt pre-positioning at Hyatt Regency Pune, W Hyderabad and Courtyard Pune openings?
qa_highlights.answer: Grand Hyatt repositioning is not being pursued. W Hyderabad is targeted for full operation in 2H FY28 or calendar 2027, with regulatory delays possible. Courtyard Pune public areas and guest room renovation is deferred to about April 2027 for 5-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Karan Gupta (Asit C Mehta): How does RARE revenue recognition work, and what are RARE's revenue, margin and EBITDA targets?
qa_highlights.answer: RARE earns booking commission and, in some hotels, higher revenue share akin to franchise fees; hotel room revenue stays with owners. Management guides Rs 100-120 crore top line at about 35% margin and Rs 35-40 crore EBITDA once stabilised in about 1.5-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Viraj Mahadevia (Moneygrow): Can RARE ROCE double the group's roughly 10%, and why is EBITDA flat while PBT is up 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RARE could reach 5x group ROCE and target 50%-55% ROCE, with about 95% EBITDA-to-PBT flow-through and no finance cost. On EBITDA, it cited the Rs 9 crore one-time other income in the prior-year base and about Rs 9 crore GST drag, with YoY relief from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Gianani (MC Research): Does the annual enabling resolution overhang equity, and how is ROCE on acquisitions in a costlier market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said such provisions are common among capital-intensive peers and no debt-equity mix has been decided. It said acquisitions still target operationally distressed assets, even at market peaks, with renovation, rebranding and asset management as the value levers.

qa_highlights.question: Ashish (Leo Capital): What is the Navi Mumbai status, timeline and capex phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said legacy issues are resolved, with statutory approvals expected in the next few months and design work to be presented next quarter. On-site start is targeted for 1 April 2027, with a 3-4 year build, capex small through FY28, and main spend in FY29-FY30.

qa_highlights.answer: Internal data show Holiday Inn Express HITEC City at 20-25% premium to portfolio average (~INR5,000-5,100 vs INR4,000); W could exceed INR170-odd crores top line, >10% of FY27 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: RARE India revenue and EBITDA outlook?

543985|2026-03.headline: Zaggle FY26 standalone revenue rose about 42% to INR1,853 crores, but FY27 standalone growth guidance slows to 25-30% as DICE moves to an asset purchase.
543985|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 results, with standalone revenue of about INR1,853 crores (up 42%) and PAT of about INR133 crores (up 52%). Q4 standalone revenue was about INR593 crores (up 44%) with reported EBITDA of about INR55 crores. The DICE acquisition was restructured from a 100% share purchase (originally INR123 crores) to an asset purchase for about INR68 crores excluding GST, which moves its costs onto the standalone P&L. Management withheld EBITDA guidance until integration completes, and cash flow is now the top priority, with operating cash flow about minus INR6 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Zaggle core (Save, Propel, Zoyer)
segments.commentary: Program fees were about 41% of revenue and SaaS about 2% in FY26. Zoyer and BROME drove a significant rise in interchange fees. Management is deliberately reducing redemption-led Propel models that absorb cash, and expects Propel margin to recover toward about 5.5% from about 4% in Q4.

segments.name: 86400 (formerly Mobileware)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR34 crores in FY25 to about INR74 crores in FY26 (up 118%). EBITDA rose from about INR5.4 crores to about INR18 crores and PAT from about INR1.6 crores to INR11 crores, driven by UPI volumes and new bank partners.

segments.name: GreenEdge
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR36.5 crores in FY25 to about INR103.7 crores in FY26 (up about 184%). EBITDA rose from about INR3.4 crores to about INR11 crores and PAT from INR2.1 crores to about INR8.1 crores. Standalone revenue growth of 40-50% is projected for FY27.

segments.name: Zagg.money (formerly Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: New acquisition for retail credit cards on UPI and TPAP. Management reports an annualised run rate of about 36,000-40,000 new cards, with a base of about 25,000 cardholders. Revenue is referral fees and interchange share with no balance-sheet risk.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (to be rebranded Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Management said performance was unsatisfactory last year. Rebranding and a Tax AI copilot launch are planned for Q2 FY27, and Quesscorp partnership covers a base of 5 lakh-plus users.

segments.commentary: Acquired as a spend management suite, IP and enterprise contracts for about INR68 crores excluding GST, against an original INR123 crores share-purchase valuation. DICE was loss-making in FY25 and likely in FY26; FY25 revenue was about INR10 crores, with FY26 described as significantly higher. Around 100-plus team members join.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated operating cash flow about minus INR52 crores versus about minus INR6 crores standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiaries are nascent businesses recently acquired, with investments made and efficiency gains to come.

qa_highlights.question: Does DICE dilute the EBITDA run rate and the 11-12% margin path?

qa_highlights.question: Is Propel worth keeping given its low net revenue and working-capital use?

543985|2026-06.headline: Zaggle Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 28% YoY to INR423 crore, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% from 10.1% on DICE costs and expensed capitalisation.

Crossover 4 PE fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Private credit first fund targets INR1,000-1,500 crore. Public markets roughly flat net flows.

segments.name: Asset Services
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR209 crore, above Q1 INR193 crore. FY26 revenue +12%, profit about +14-15%. Domestic RTA and trusteeship services expected live by mid-Q3 FY27. Global-local custodian tie-up on the verge of signing. Market share about 22% of chosen segments.

segments.name: Capital Markets (IB and IE)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR138 crore. Equity cash ADT -6%, futures ADT -14%, options +8% for FY26. IPO market share 19% by value and 15% by deals. Fixed income revenue +34-35% YoY, now about 50% of IB. IB/IE split about 30:70.

guidance_outlook: Asset services yields expected to hold at current levels; a possible rise over 12-15 months if inflation stays sticky and rates rise.
Wealth cost-to-income expected to fall about 100 bps a year over 3-4 years, with management choosing how much productivity gain to reinvest in RMs.
Private ARR yield expected to average 90-95 bps.
Management expects a good year in investment banking in FY27, with a 40-45 live mandate pipeline.
FY27 will carry incremental asset management costs for new strategies and the MF/SIF launch, which management calls investment rather than run-rate cost.
Bank guarantee norms expected to cost about INR10-15 crore a year net of deposit costs.
Private credit fund launch by end Q2 FY27; commercial real estate fund launch in H2 FY27 targeting INR3,000-3,500 crore (other remarks cite INR3,000-4,000 crore).
SIF launch expected after MF license, roughly two to three months from now.
capex_capacity: Commercial real estate fund: about INR3,800 crore raised by Q4; 40-50% deployed; three assets acquired (about 3.8 mn sq ft). New fund launch once about 70% deployed, expected H2 FY27.
Private equity Crossover 4 fund: about INR250-275 crore raised so far, target INR1,000-1,500 crore over the next 6-10 months.
Private credit: CIO Amit Kansal appointed; first fund targeting INR1,000-1,500 crore, launch by end Q2 FY27.
Virasat estate and legacy planning service launched; agentic AI tools deployed for RMs.
Asset services: RTA and trusteeship go-live expected by mid-Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: Net flows in Wealth ran at 30% of opening MPIS assets; Private net flows about 22% of opening assets, in line with guidance.
Regret attrition: Private about 1-2%, Wealth about 3-4%. Management says AUM loss is limited.
Wealth RM productivity up about 25% YoY, helped by a lower share of under-one-year RMs (from 40-45% to about 33%) and AI tools. Private revenue per RM up 10-15% from agentic AI.
Private transactional revenue up 14% in FY26 vs ARR up 32%. Transactional revenue is about 90-95% broking and fixed income, with the rest deals.
Insurance volume growth moderated to about 25-30% from about 50%; management reports no yield impact. Category 2 mix may rise in volatile markets.
Industry view: new entrants offer high RM payouts, which management calls a caution; consolidation expected, with a few scale multiproduct leaders.
Mutual fund commission cut (April 1): management says impact negligible, as MF is under 20% of IE revenue and pass-through is similar to proposal.
Public markets: gross flows offset by redemptions, net flat for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How should ECM revenue share be modelled for FY27 given large upcoming IPOs, and what is the impact of the MF commission cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 40-45 live ECM and advisory mandates, and Q4 deal slippage is expected to recover. MF commission cut impact is hardly material, as MF is under 20% of IE revenue and net margins are similar.

qa_highlights.question: Is the asset services yield at risk as rates fall, and what drove the higher cash share?
qa_highlights.answer: Yields should hold, as rate cuts have already flowed through. The cash share rose after a large client was replaced by many smaller clients; the portfolio mix is about 70:30 to 75:25. A rate hike would lift yields as deposits reprice.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% wealth productivity gain from AI or from mix, and how do clients per RM evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes it to RM seasoning (under-one-year share fell to about 33%) plus AI tools. Net new money is the outcome, not the cause of productivity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for transactional revenue in FY27 and the insurance commission trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Transactional revenue is mostly broking and fixed income, which are insulated from geopolitics. Insurance yields are steady, with some first-year commission support from category 2 products.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income ratios evolve in Wealth?
qa_highlights.answer: Wealth CTI fell 130-150 bps this year. Management guides about 100 bps a year over 3-4 years, with reinvestment in RM capacity as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 asset management flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: PE Crossover 4 targets INR1,000-1,500 crore; private credit first fund INR1,000-1,500 crore with about half this year; CRE fund INR3,000-4,000 crore with 30-40% this year. SIF flow numbers to be discussed next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the Ultra-HNI book sits above INR10 crore, and what is the mix of wealth clients by geography?
qa_highlights.answer: Families above INR10 crore are about one-third of the total and contribute 70-75% of AUM. Tier 2 and beyond is 35-40% of Nuvama Wealth. Private: top 8 cities about 80-85%.

risks_watch: Capital market revenue cyclicality: ECM and QIP volumes softened in H2 FY26, and Q4 deals slipped.
Asset services sensitivity to rates and collateral mix; rate direction could move yields either way.
Competitive intensity from new wealth entrants offering high RM payouts; RM attrition (regret attrition about 3-4% in Wealth).
Incremental asset management costs in FY27 for MF/SIF launch and new strategies.
Execution on SIF/MF license (final inspection done), private credit fund launch and RTA/trusteeship go-live by mid-Q3 FY27.
NII lag: loan book up 27% but NII growth lagged due to ECL provisioning; processing-fee acceleration expected in Q1 FY27.
Geopolitical volatility (West Asia) and the impact on ESOP-linked lending and client flows.

financial_highlights.change: +7% YoY; +13% YoY excluding IE and IB
FY26 ex-IE and IB revenue +17% YoY
Q4 up 9% YoY; FY25 revenue +41% with cost +24%
Q1 FY26 was INR193 crore; FY26 revenue +12%

financial_highlights.metric: IB and IE revenue, Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Up 22% (ARR now about 60% of Private revenue)

key_quotes: For us, it was a complete test of resilience this year. We navigated multiple moving parts, including something specific for us and overall macro uncertainty.
I don't think that this business one should rush in because one bad performance here can have years of negative impact.
I don't think the yield will compress because we've seen a decline in the overall interest rates happen and that flow-through has largely happened.
Next quarter, we could discuss the numbers. And by that time, maybe the volatility levels of the market also should settle down.

It was evasive on the exact yield outlook and gave no firm numbers on the SIF and mutual fund flows, deferring them to next quarter.
